title: Versioned v3.0.0 upgrade path is missing 4 tables and ~25 columns that instrumentation.ts creates
description: Live-verified: built a true v2.0.0-shaped scratch DB (34 tables, from the frozen instrumentation-v2.ts snapshot) with seed data, ran the real db:migrate engine to 3.0.0 (41/41 steps succeeded), then diffed the result against instrumentation.ts. Missing tables: processed_stripe_events, user_ai_configs, cve_kev_cache, webhook_deliveries. Missing columns include api_keys.scopes; users.ai_chat_banned/google_id/google_email/google_name/google_avatar_url/github_id/github_email/github_name/github_avatar_url/discord_username/discord_avatar_url/discord_email/scans_private_by_default; scan_history.share_expires_at/is_public; broadcast_messages.sent_by; scheduled_scans.preferred_hour_utc/preferred_day_of_week/preferred_day_of_month; webhooks.secret; host_reputation.findings/response_headers/result_meta/authenticated/scanned_url; plus idx_scan_history_url_public_completed. db:migrate against real production tonight will write schema_version=3.0.0 to vulnradar_schema_meta while these remain absent -- it only flips a version flag, it does not fully upgrade the schema.
recommendation: Add the missing addTables/addColumns entries to 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs, the matching table/column names to _registry.mjs's v3.0.0 fingerprint, and the 4 new table names to create-fresh-db.mjs's MIGRATE_TABLES v3.0.0-only list. Re-run the scratch-DB round-trip to confirm zero drift before trusting db:migrate against production.

title: The migration runner, the fresh-install builder, and the restore script total 5,574 untested lines, and scripts/ is excluded from coverage so none of that gap is visible in any report
category: data-loss tooling with no test and no coverage measurement
description: scripts/ holds 13,161 lines across 58 files and vitest.config.ts excludes it twice over: coverage.include is only ["lib/**/*.ts", "app/**/*.ts"] (line 31) and coverage.exclude lists "scripts/**" (line 37). So the 20 test files under tests/scripts/ run but produce no measurable coverage, and the untested remainder is invisible. Mapping tests to sources by hand: scripts/migrate/ is 4,431 lines and tests/scripts/migrate/ contains exactly one file, versions/2.0.0-to-3.0.0.test.ts. That leaves migrate.mjs (577 lines, the entry point), _registry.mjs (637), _planner.mjs (246, decides which steps run and in what order), _runner.mjs (152, executes them), _detect.mjs (84, decides the installed version), _meta.mjs (82), versions/1.0.0-to-2.0.0.mjs (174), versions/2.0.0-to-1.0.0.mjs (the deliberate downgrade, 59), _legacy-original.mjs (871), and _snippets.mjs (241) with no test at all. scripts/create-fresh-db/ (1,023 lines plus two schema files) has no test. scripts/restore-db.mjs (120 lines) has no test, although scripts/backup-db.mjs does (tests/scripts/backup-db.test.ts). scripts/db-repair-sequences.mjs has none.
impact: These are the only scripts in the repo that run destructive DDL and DML against a populated production database, and the two least covered are the two that matter most: _planner/_detect decide which migration steps run against a live install (a wrong version detection runs the wrong step, or reruns one), and restore-db.mjs is the recovery path an operator reaches for on their worst day. A broken restore is discovered exactly when it cannot be fixed. The coverage exclusion compounds this: an operator or reviewer running `npm run test:coverage` sees an 81% line figure that says nothing about this 5,574-line surface.
recommendation: Two changes. First, in vitest.config.ts add "scripts/**/*.mjs" to coverage.include and delete "scripts/**" from coverage.exclude so the gap is measurable. Second, add tests using the existing tests/scripts/_pg-mock.ts harness for: _detect.mjs (each version-detection branch and the ambiguous case), _planner.mjs (the step sequence for every from/to pair including the 2.0.0-to-1.0.0 downgrade, and that an unknown version refuses to plan), _runner.mjs (a failing step aborts and does not continue), and restore-db.mjs (refuses a truncated or wrong-schema dump, and does not drop the existing database before the dump validates).

title: The versioned v3.0.0 upgrade path is missing 11 tables and 8 columns that instrumentation.ts creates, so db:migrate stamps schema_version=3.0.0 on a schema that is not 3.0.0
category: migration path diverges from the boot-time schema
description: instrumentation.ts contains 64 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements (63 app tables plus vulnradar_schema_meta). The complete set a database can reach through the migration engine is the 19-table v1 baseline plus the 33 tables created across scripts/migrate/versions/1.0.0-to-2.0.0.mjs, 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs and _snippets.mjs, so 52 app tables plus the meta table. Diffing the two sets, these 11 tables exist only on the boot path and are created by no migration step at all: browserbase_credit_purchases (instrumentation.ts:3094), browserbase_usage (3075), domains (3173), email_logs (671), github_credit_purchases (3024), scan_screenshots (1377), support_ticket_messages (3446), support_ticket_shares (3460), support_tickets (3430), user_avatars (1411), worker_failure_state (3136). Eight columns are in the same position: sessions.impersonated_by (347), sessions.ipv4_address (352), finding_remediation.due_at (1515), host_reputation.auto_tags (1840), users.billing_interval (2683), users.github_credit_balance (2827), users.browserbase_credit_seconds_balance (3061), ai_credit_purchases.refunded_at (3117). None of these names appear in _registry.mjs's v3.0.0 fingerprint (scripts/migrate/_registry.mjs:213) either. This is the exact defect AUDIT-009#migration-01 recorded as critical and whose fix comment in this same file (line 52) says it was closed "for good"; it has re-opened at 11 tables, larger than the original 4.
impact: npm run db:migrate is the documented upgrade command (app/docs/setup/page.tsx:495, app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:547) and the last step the in-app self-updater runs (components/admin/features/updater-manager.tsx:65). After it completes it writes schema_version=3.0.0 via writeMeta (scripts/migrate/migrate.mjs:550) and reports success, while the database is missing the tables behind support tickets, custom domains, avatars, screenshots, email delivery logs, the worker failure watchdog and all three credit-purchase ledgers. The only thing that closes the gap is the app's next boot, which the self-updater deliberately does not trigger ("It does not build or restart the server"), and each of those boot-time creates is individually .catch-guarded as non-fatal, so a failure there is a single console.error and the app serves traffic with tables missing. An operator who trusts schema_version, or who uses db:migrate to prepare a database the app has not yet booted against, has an incomplete schema with no signal that anything is wrong.
recommendation: Add the 11 missing tables to 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs's addTables (copying the DDL verbatim from instrumentation.ts, in FK-safe order: support_tickets before its messages/shares, domains after teams) and the 8 missing columns to addColumns, with matching entries in the downgrade's dropTables/dropColumns. Add every one of those table and column names to _registry.mjs's v3.0.0 fingerprint. Then fix the structural cause via migrate-09 and migrate-10 so this cannot silently re-open a third time.

title: db:create's data copy omits 33 of the 63 app tables, including system_settings, access_rules, webhooks and support_tickets, and never reports them as skipped
category: silent data loss in the clone/migrate path
description: MIGRATE_TABLES is a hardcoded 30-entry list. migrateData (line 471) builds its work set as MIGRATE_TABLES.filter(t => targetSet.has(t)) and showDataMigrationPlan (line 509) iterates `for (const table of MIGRATE_TABLES)`. Both loops are driven entirely by that list, so a table that exists in the source database and in the target schema but is absent from MIGRATE_TABLES is never copied and never appears in either the plan or the post-run report. The cannotCopy branch (line 489) only warns about entries that ARE in MIGRATE_TABLES but missing from the target, which is the opposite case. Diffing MIGRATE_TABLES against instrumentation.ts's CREATE TABLE set, these 33 app tables are never copied: access_rules, admin_user_notes, ai_credit_purchases, ai_usage, api_usage, billing_verification_codes, broadcast_messages, broadcast_recipients, browserbase_credit_purchases, browserbase_usage, data_requests, device_trust, discord_connections, domains, email_2fa_codes, email_logs, email_verification_tokens, github_credit_purchases, host_badges, notification_preferences, promoted_auto_tag_rules, rate_limits, scan_screenshots, security_alerts, staff_activity, subdomain_cache, support_ticket_messages, support_ticket_shares, support_tickets, system_settings, user_avatars, webhooks, worker_failure_state.
impact: npm run db:create is documented as the way to move to a different database, including production (app/docs/setup/page.tsx:735, app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:274, app/docs/developers/page.tsx:575). An operator who clones and cuts over silently loses every admin-configured runtime setting (system_settings), the IP whitelist/blacklist (access_rules), every user's outbound webhook configuration (webhooks), every notification preference, every Discord link, every trusted device, every open support ticket and its messages and shares, every custom domain, every uploaded avatar (user_avatars), every embedded badge token (host_badges, so live third-party embeds start 404ing), every purchased AI/GitHub/Browserbase credit ledger row, and every open GDPR data request. The plan screen shown before the operator approves lists none of these as at risk, so the loss is invisible both before and after.
recommendation: In create-fresh-db.mjs, stop driving the copy from a hardcoded list. Enumerate the source database's public tables, topologically order them by their declared foreign keys, and copy every table that exists in the target. Keep an explicit SKIP_TABLES list only for genuinely transient data (rate_limits, email_2fa_codes, password_reset_tokens, email_verification_tokens, subdomain_cache, cve_kev_cache) and print that skip list in showDataMigrationPlan. At minimum, add an assertion that every source table with rows is either in MIGRATE_TABLES or in SKIP_TABLES, and fail the run rather than silently dropping it.

title: repairAllSequences setvals every sequence down to MAX(id) with no forward-only guard, unlike the copy in instrumentation.ts, and runs post-COMMIT against a live database
category: duplicated logic that has provably drifted
description: There are two implementations of the same operation. instrumentation.ts:3577-3593 reads pg_sequence_last_value into seqVal, reads MAX(col) into maxVal, and only calls setval when `maxVal > 0 && maxVal > seqVal`, so it can only move a sequence forward. scripts/migrate/_runner.mjs's repairAllSequences runs a DO block that reads only `COALESCE(MAX(%I), 0)` and then, guarded by `IF max_val > 0`, unconditionally runs `setval(seq, max_val)` with no comparison against the sequence's current value. It therefore moves a sequence BACKWARDS whenever rows above MAX(id) have been deleted. This function runs in three places against real databases: _runner.mjs:137 immediately after COMMIT on every real migration, migrate.mjs:537 on every same-version no-op re-run, and db-repair-sequences.mjs:37. The self-updater's last step is `npm run db:migrate` executed from inside the running app with no restart (app/api/v3/admin/updater/apply/route.ts:28, components/admin/features/updater-manager.tsx:65), so this setval runs outside any transaction while the app is still inserting rows. Read MAX(id)=N, concurrent app INSERT consumes nextval N+1 and commits, setval(N) executes, the next app INSERT gets nextval N+1 again and fails with duplicate key value violates unique constraint. Separately, the backwards move means ids of deleted rows get handed out again: scan_history rows are pruned by lib/database/cleanup.ts:154-200 and by user deletion cascade, and AUDIT-012#authz-09 records that scan screenshots are readable with no authentication by that sequential id.
impact: Every release applied through the admin self-updater runs this against production while the app is serving. The narrow window produces a duplicate-key 500 on a live scan insert; the sequence rewind causes primary-key reuse on scan_history, admin_audit_log, security_alerts, user_notifications and every other SERIAL table after any deletion, so a stale sequential-id reference (a screenshot URL, a stored API integration id) can resolve to a different row belonging to a different user. The function's own header says its purpose is to fix a sequence that "fell behind", which is the forward case only, so the backwards behavior is not intended.
recommendation: In scripts/migrate/_runner.mjs's repairAllSequences, select `pg_sequence_last_value(s.oid)` alongside the sequence in the cursor and change the body to `IF max_val > 0 AND max_val > COALESCE(last_val, 0) THEN ... END IF`, matching instrumentation.ts:3589. Better, delete the duplicate entirely and export the guarded implementation from one shared module that both instrumentation.ts and the migrate scripts import. Also stop calling it inside runPlan when the app may be live, or take a `pg_advisory_lock` around it.

title: GET /api/v3/badge/[token] joins scan_history on url with no usable index, so the most hotlinked public endpoint in the product does a sequential scan of the whole scans table per request
category: missing index on a public hot path
description: The badge route runs `FROM host_badges hb JOIN scan_history sh ON sh.url = hb.url AND (sh.user_id = hb.user_id OR (hb.scope = 'global' AND sh.is_public = true)) WHERE hb.badge_token_hash = $1 AND hb.revoked_at IS NULL AND sh.status = 'completed' ORDER BY sh.scanned_at DESC LIMIT 1` (app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts:66-74). The only index touching `scan_history.url` is `idx_scan_history_url_public_completed ON scan_history(url) WHERE is_public = true AND status = 'completed'` (instrumentation.ts:2359-2361). Because the `sh.user_id = hb.user_id` half of the OR is deliberately NOT gated on `is_public` (see the comment at app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:51-52), the query's predicate does not imply the index's partial predicate and Postgres cannot use it. There is no unconditional index on `scan_history(url)`. The identical join shape appears at app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:59-67 and app/api/v3/shared/[token]/screenshot/route.ts:50-57.
impact: A status badge is an embedded in third-party READMEs and websites; it is by construction the highest-request-rate route in the app and it is unauthenticated. Every hit currently seq-scans scan_history. At 10k scan rows that is already tens of milliseconds of pure I/O per badge render; it degrades linearly forever and there is no cache in front of it.
recommendation: Add `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_scan_history_url_scanned ON scan_history(url, scanned_at DESC);` to the performance-index block in instrumentation.ts (near line 1587). The same index also serves the `DISTINCT ON (url) ... ORDER BY url, scanned_at DESC` sorts in app/api/v3/badge/scans/route.ts:24-31 and lib/notifications/posture-digest.ts:81-91, and the `WHERE user_id = $1 AND url = $2 ORDER BY scanned_at DESC LIMIT 1` lookup in lib/scanner/regression-alert.ts:63-65 that runs after every completed scan.

title: The AI chat launcher covers the Save Changes button on /profile and the bottom-right of every commerce form
description: components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:1613-1617 renders a 56px FAB at bottom-5 right-5 z-50, mounted after children. Its route gating at :1273-1284 returns null on /browser/, /docs and /admin, but not /profile. At 375px the save card spans to right:16px with right-aligned buttons, so the FAB occupying right 20-76px and y 20-76px sits directly over Save Changes.
impact: Compounds shell-02 on /profile: even after dismissing the cookie notice, the chat launcher still covers the save button on a phone. Also covers the bottom-right of forms on /pricing, /checkout, /contact, /legal and the auth pages.
recommendation: Offset the launcher by --vr-cookie-h and give the floating save bars right padding that clears 76px on mobile, or add /profile to the launcher's null-return route list.

title: Boot-time schema catch-up in instrumentation.ts is the only thing that closes the migration-01 gap for an existing prod DB, and one failed statement silently aborts everything after it
description: instrumentation.ts's entire ~1700-line schema-creation/seed/cleanup-scheduling/sequence-repair sequence is wrapped in exactly one outer try/catch that only console.error's on failure and never calls process.exit -- the app continues booting and serving production traffic regardless. Most v3-era CREATE TABLE/ALTER TABLE calls are bare awaits with no individual try/catch, unlike the FK self-heal blocks and a handful of blocks that ARE wrapped in .catch(). Since this boot sequence is the ONLY mechanism that actually creates the tables/columns missing from the versioned migration, a single unexpected failure partway through it silently abandons every later table, every later column, badge seeding, periodic cleanup scheduling, and the sequence-repair safety net, with no forced restart and no alert beyond one buried log line.
recommendation: Wrap each independent v3-era schema block in its own try/catch, matching the pattern already used for the FK self-heal blocks; consider having the top-level catch call process.exit(1) instead of only logging, so a broken schema never silently serves production traffic.

title: Half of .github/labeler.yml uses an invented schema the labeler action silently ignores, so the step named "Apply size label" has never applied a size label
description: actions/labeler takes the label name as the top-level key and accepts only `changed-files`, `base-branch`, `head-branch`, `any` and `all` as matcher keys. .github/labeler.yml gets this right for four blocks (`ci` line 24, `config` line 29, `security` line 35, `docs` line 39) and wrong for the other two. The `size` block (lines 3-16) has a top-level key `size` whose entries are `{label: "size/xs", files: [...]}`, and the `dependencies` block (lines 18-21) uses `{label: "dependencies", from-branch: [...]}`. `label`, `files` and `from-branch` are not matcher keys. I confirmed against the action's source (src/api/get-label-configs.ts): an unrecognised key is not an error, it hits `core.info(\`An unknown config option was under ${label}: ${key}\`)` and produces no matcher, so the labels `size`, `size/xs`, `size/s`, `size/m`, `size/l` and the branch-based `dependencies` rule are never applied. The step at .github/workflows/label.yml:16 is literally named "Apply size label". Separately, label.yml:7-8 declares `permissions: pull-requests: write` only; declaring any permission sets every unlisted scope to `none`, including `contents`, while the action's documented usage requires `contents: read` to read the configuration file from the repository.
impact: PR triage silently does not work. Maintainers see no size labels, and the `dependencies` label the stale.yml exemption logic and the auto-merge ignore flow both reason about is never applied from the branch name (dependabot supplies it from .github/dependabot.yml:12-14 instead, which masks the breakage). Nothing in the log makes this visible except an `info`-level line nobody reads.
recommendation: Rewrite the `size` and `dependencies` blocks in .github/labeler.yml to the real schema: one top-level key per label (`size/xs:`, `size/s:`, ...) with `- changed-files: - any-glob-to-any-file: [...]`, and `dependencies: - head-branch: ["^dependabot/"]`. Note that labeler matches on paths, not diff size, so if a real size label is wanted use a line-count action instead. Add `contents: read` to the permissions block in .github/workflows/label.yml:7.

title: The security badge is the product's only backlink loop and every badge points at a /shared/ URL that is Disallowed in robots.txt and served noindex, nofollow, so the inbound links are thrown away
description: app/docs/sharing/page.tsx:386 publishes the embed snippet users paste onto their own sites: ``. Both halves of that snippet point at paths that robots.txt forbids: `/shared/` via lib/seo/routes.ts:121 and `/api/` via line 108, both spread into the wildcard Disallow at app/robots.ts:60. On top of that the link target itself serves `noindex, nofollow` (app/shared/[token]/layout.tsx:7 via privatePageMetadata, lib/seo/metadata.ts:85). So the destination cannot be crawled, cannot be indexed, and carries nofollow. The image is an SVG served from /api/v3/badge/[token] (app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts:122, Content-Type image/svg+xml), which is also Disallowed and which social and image crawlers do not render.
impact: A security badge on a customer's site is the standard organic-growth loop for this product category: it is how Security Headers, SSL Labs and Mozilla Observatory accumulate their link graph. Here the feature is built, documented, and produces a link that search engines are explicitly told to ignore. Every customer who installs a badge gives the product a link worth nothing.
recommendation: Point the documented `<a href>` at `/host/<hostname>` instead of `/shared/<token>`: it is the stable, per-host public page for the same site (app/api/v3/host/[hostname]/route.ts only ever serves public scans, and its host_reputation row is deleted when a scan is made private), it does not expose a token in someone else's page source, and it is the page a stranger arriving from the badge actually wants. Then do seo-09 so that target is indexable and followable. Update the snippet at app/docs/sharing/page.tsx:386 and anywhere the badge UI generates the same HTML. Keep the SVG badge image where it is; the link, not the image, is what carries the value.

title: /host/[hostname] is kept noindex and robots-Disallowed on the stated grounds that the URL space is "not enumerable", which is false: host_reputation is a table and /public-scans already paginates it
description: lib/seo/routes.ts:100-106 justifies excluding /host/ and /shared/ together: "Tokenised or per-entity URLs (/shared/<token>, /browser/<id>, /host/<hostname>). Not enumerable ahead of time, so there is no fixed list to publish a sitemap entry or canonical for." That reasoning is correct for /shared/<token> and /browser/<id>, which are secrets. It is not correct for /host/<hostname>: app/api/v3/host/[hostname]/route.ts:99 reads from the `host_reputation` table keyed on `host`, so the full list is a single SELECT, and app/public-scans/page.tsx already renders a paginated, sitemapped, indexable directory of exactly this data. The data is public by construction, not by accident: app/api/v3/host/[hostname]/route.ts:140 gates the live findings on `is_public = true`, and the route's own comment states the host_reputation row is deleted when its source scan is made private. The page also already has a per-host trend chart (components/host/danger-score-trend.tsx). Today the page ships privatePageMetadata("Host Report", "/host") (app/host/[hostname]/layout.tsx:8), so it has no per-host title, no per-host description, a canonical pointing at /host which is not a route, and noindex.
impact: "<domain> security report" and "is <domain> safe" are the highest-volume query shapes in this product category, and they are the entire organic strategy of Security Headers, SSL Labs, Mozilla Observatory and urlscan.io. The product already generates the pages that answer them, already restricts them to public data, already links them from an indexable directory, and then blocks all of them. The 749 /checks pages target "how to fix X" intent, which converts worse: someone searching a check name is fixing a problem they already found, while someone searching a domain is looking for a scanner.
recommendation: Three changes. (1) Replace app/host/[hostname]/layout.tsx with an async generateMetadata({ params }) that resolves the host via the same host_reputation lookup and returns pageMetadata({ title: `${host} security report`, description: `${host} scored ${dangerScore}/10 on ${date}: ${critical} critical and ${high} high findings across headers, TLS, cookies and DNS.`, path: `/host/${host}`, noIndex: !known || findings.length === 0 }), so an unscanned or empty host stays noindex and only real reports are indexable. (2) Remove "/host/" from DISALLOWED_PATHS in lib/seo/routes.ts:122, leaving "/shared/" and "/browser/" in place. (3) Publish the URLs: add a second sitemap (Next 15 supports generateSitemaps(), or a plain app/sitemap-hosts.xml/route.ts) that selects host and last_scanned_at from host_reputation and emits a real per-host lastmod, and reference both from a sitemap index. Note app/sitemap.ts is currently `force-static` so the host sitemap must be a separate dynamic route. Pair with seo-02 so each host page also gets a real social card, and with seo-08 so badges point here.

title: No test in the repo executes real SQL: 192 of 356 test files mock the pg pool and there is no test database, so column typos, broken CTEs, missing row locks, and schema drift are all invisible
description: Scope: the whole suite plus vitest.config.ts and the schema. 192 of the 356 test files contain `vi.mock("@/lib/database/db")`, and 195 reference a fake pool shape. Nothing in the repo starts a Postgres: no docker-compose service for tests, no testcontainers dependency, and the only tests that read DATABASE_URL do so to assert configuration behaviour, not to connect. Even tests/lib/database/db.test.ts, which cannot mock the module it tests, mocks one level lower at pg's Pool class with a FakePool. The result is that every SQL string in lib/ and app/ is treated as an opaque token: a mocked client returns whatever the test scripted regardless of what the query says, so a wrong column name, a dropped WHERE clause, a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` that lost its lock, or a CTE that no longer returns its RETURNING row all pass. instrumentation.ts, the canonical schema at 3,639 lines with 72 CREATE TABLE and 97 CREATE INDEX statements, is explicitly excluded from coverage (vitest.config.ts:38) and only two test files reference it at all. There is also a documented contradiction: CLAUDE.md lists 'Mocking the database in tests' under What to avoid, while tests/README.md instructs 'Mock at the network and database boundary, not below it', and the suite follows the README.
impact: This is the structural reason a whole class of AUDIT-012 findings existed. Credit-ledger atomicity, the nine missing indexes in AUDIT-012#perf-15 that force full scans inside the cleanup transaction, and the function-wrapped columns in AUDIT-012#perf-16 that defeat an index are all properties of SQL text that the suite by construction cannot evaluate. The failure mode in production is a query that throws at runtime on a column that no longer exists, or an aggregate that returns silently wrong numbers, after a green CI run and a green deploy.
recommendation: Do not rewrite 192 files. Add one narrow integration suite gated on an env var, tests/integration/, that spins Postgres in the CI test job as a services: container, runs instrumentation.ts to build the schema, and exercises only the queries where correctness cannot be asserted any other way: the credit ledger reversals, reserveConcurrentScanSlot, incrementDailyCountCapped, and lib/database/cleanup.ts. Then resolve the doc contradiction by amending CLAUDE.md to match what the project actually does, so the next contributor is not choosing between two rules.

title: The schema-version marker is written in a third separate transaction after the DDL commit, so an interruption between them leaves a fully migrated database the app refuses to boot on
category: version marker not atomic with the change it records
description: A migration reaches durability in three independent commits. First runPlan (scripts/migrate/_runner.mjs:83) opens one transaction, runs every plan step, and COMMITs at line 134. Second, still inside runPlan at line 137, `await repairAllSequences(client)` runs as its own autocommit statement with no try/catch. Third, control returns to migrate.mjs, which only reaches `await writeMeta(livePool, {...})` at line 550 if runPlan returned normally. So an exception from repairAllSequences, a killed process, or a dropped connection anywhere after the COMMIT leaves the schema fully upgraded while vulnradar_schema_meta still holds the old version. instrumentation.ts:148-190 then compares that stale version against MIN_SCHEMA_VERSION ("3.0.0", lib/config/config-values.ts:28) and calls process.exit(1) with a SCHEMA VERSION MISMATCH box. This extends AUDIT-009#migration-03, which reported the unguarded repairAllSequences call as a confusing false failure message; that call is still unguarded at _runner.mjs:137 and at migrate.mjs:537. What is new here is the structural point the false message is a symptom of: writeMeta is not in the same transaction as the DDL it records, and the consequence is not a confusing log line but a hard boot refusal.
impact: The app will not start at all, on a database that is actually correct, until someone re-runs db:migrate. Because the self-updater runs db:migrate as its last step from inside the running app, the operator's next restart is the moment this surfaces, with the misleading message that the database schema is older than the app requires. Re-running db:migrate does recover (every step is idempotent), but only if the operator ignores the message telling them the schema is behind.
recommendation: Move the writeMeta INSERT into runPlan's transaction: pass the target version and app version into runPlan and issue the vulnradar_schema_meta upsert as the last statement before COMMIT, so schema and version marker commit or roll back together. Move repairAllSequences after that COMMIT and wrap it in its own try/catch that warns without failing the run.

title: Two indexes are UNIQUE on the boot path and non-unique on the migration path, and CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS means whichever runs first wins
category: index definition drift between the two schema sources
description: The upgrade's addIndexes entry at 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs:999-1003 is expanded by scripts/migrate/_planner.mjs:140 into `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_github_connections_github_user_id ON "github_connections"(github_user_id)`, a plain non-unique index. instrumentation.ts:1933 creates an index with the identical NAME as `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_github_connections_github_user_id ON github_connections(github_user_id)`. IF NOT EXISTS matches on the index name only, not its definition, so whichever path runs first permanently decides whether the constraint exists, and the other silently no-ops. db:migrate is documented and scripted to run before the app boots, so on any migrated database the index is non-unique. The same shape applies to idx_host_badges_token_hash: non-unique and partial at 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs:1019-1024 (`WHERE badge_token_hash IS NOT NULL`) versus `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` with no predicate at instrumentation.ts:3387.
impact: github_connections has no other constraint on github_user_id (the table's only UNIQUE is on user_id, see 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs:333, and lib/github/github-connections.ts:103 upserts on ON CONFLICT (user_id)). On a fresh-boot database, a second VulnRadar account connecting the same GitHub identity fails with a unique violation; on a migrated database it succeeds. Two accounts can then both hold an encrypted access token for one GitHub user and both consume that user's review quota, and behavior differs between two installs that both report schema_version=3.0.0. For host_badges the practical exposure is smaller because badge_token is already NOT NULL UNIQUE, but the index shape still differs between installs.
recommendation: Add a `unique: true` flag to the addIndexes step shape in scripts/migrate/_planner.mjs's expandPlan (line 139) and emit CREATE UNIQUE INDEX when set, then mark both entries in 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs unique and drop the WHERE predicate on idx_host_badges_token_hash so it matches instrumentation.ts exactly. Add a test that every `addIndexes` name in a version file resolves to an index in instrumentation.ts with the same uniqueness and predicate.

title: Both "frozen" schema snapshots are wrong: the v2.0.0 file was edited twice despite its DO NOT EDIT header, and the v1.0.0 file ships a v3-era table with a different column shape
description: scripts/create-fresh-db/schemas/instrumentation-v2.ts:2-4 says "Frozen at v2.0.0" and "DO NOT EDIT". It contains 37 CREATE TABLE statements. The registry's v2.0.0 fingerprint (scripts/migrate/_registry.mjs:114-151) is 34 tables. The three extras are support_tickets (instrumentation-v2.ts:567), support_ticket_messages and support_ticket_shares, added by commits db113cfb "feat(support): in-app support ticket backend" and eae5e781 "feat(support): share a ticket with specific teammates", both v3.7-era work. Separately, scripts/create-fresh-db/schemas/instrumentation-v1.ts:389 creates processed_stripe_events, which the registry lists as a v3.0.0 addition and which the v1.0.0 fingerprint (_registry.mjs:53-73, 19 tables) does not contain, and it creates it with a DIFFERENT shape than every other path: `event_id TEXT, event_type TEXT, received_at TIMESTAMP` versus instrumentation.ts:548's `event_id VARCHAR(255), event_type VARCHAR(100), processed_at TIMESTAMP`. Because both later paths use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS (instrumentation.ts:547, 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs:395), neither can ever repair the column name.
impact: AUDIT-009 proved its migration-01 fix by "building a true v2.0.0-shaped scratch DB from the frozen instrumentation-v2.ts snapshot" and diffing the migrated result against instrumentation.ts. That baseline is no longer v2.0.0, so any repeat of that verification silently excuses drift on the support-ticket tables, which is part of why migrate-01 re-opened. For the v1 path, `npm run db:create` at 1.0.0 followed by `npm run db:migrate` produces a database where processed_stripe_events has received_at instead of processed_at: instrumentation.ts's `CREATE INDEX idx_processed_stripe_events_processed_at` then errors on every boot (logged non-fatally at line 555), and app/api/v3/admin/billing-overview/route.ts:131 and :140 both select processed_at and fall into their .catch fallbacks, so the admin billing overview permanently reports zero failed payments.
recommendation: Revert the three support-ticket table blocks out of scripts/create-fresh-db/schemas/instrumentation-v2.ts and remove processed_stripe_events from instrumentation-v1.ts, restoring both to the 34-table and 19-table shapes the registry fingerprints declare. Add a test that asserts the CREATE TABLE set parsed from each snapshot equals its version's fingerprint tables exactly, so an edit to a frozen file fails CI rather than passing silently.

title: fingerprintDetect counts missing columns but never lets them disqualify a version, so a half-migrated database is detected as complete and then bricks the app at boot
category: version detection accepts an incomplete schema
description: fingerprintDetect rejects a version only when a fingerprint TABLE is missing (line 33, `if (missingTables.length > 0) continue`). Column checks at lines 38-45 accumulate a missingColumns count that is used for exactly one thing: downgrading `confidence` from "high" to "medium" at line 73. The match is still returned as the detected version. So a database with all 34 v2 tables but missing v2 columns on users (the exact state a partial or interrupted 1.0.0 to 2.0.0 run leaves) is reported as "2.0.0 (confidence: medium)". migrate.mjs:365 accepts that value with no threshold check, buildPlan("2.0.0", "3.0.0") is composed, and the 1.0.0 to 2.0.0 addColumns entries that would have supplied users.plan, stripe_customer_id, subscription_status, beta_access and daily_scan_limit (scripts/migrate/versions/1.0.0-to-2.0.0.mjs:62-119) are never run. writeMeta then stamps 3.0.0. instrumentation.ts never re-adds those columns either: they exist only inside the inline CREATE TABLE users at line 280, and there is no `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS plan` anywhere in the file.
impact: On the next boot, `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_plan ON users(plan)` at instrumentation.ts:325 raises column does not exist. That statement is inside the pool.query block starting at line 279, one of the 41 blocks with no .catch, so it reaches the outer handler at line 3618 and calls process.exit(1). The app is permanently unbootable, the operator is told schema creation failed partway through, and re-running db:migrate does not help because the meta row now says 3.0.0 so the detector never revisits the v1 to v2 columns. Recovery requires hand-editing vulnradar_schema_meta. This is precisely the case the meta table's own header (scripts/migrate/_meta.mjs:11) claims to prevent.
recommendation: In scripts/migrate/_detect.mjs, treat a non-zero missingColumns as disqualifying: `continue` past that version the same way a missing table does, so detection falls back to the highest version that is genuinely complete. Keep the medium-confidence path only for columns explicitly marked optional in the fingerprint. In migrate.mjs, refuse to proceed on a low-confidence or ambiguous detection when running non-interactively.

title: Nothing verifies the schema against the target fingerprint after a migration, even though the registry's own header says that is what fingerprints are for
description: scripts/migrate/_registry.mjs:5-8 states the migrator uses fingerprints "both for: Detecting the current version when no meta table exists [and] Verifying a target version was reached after a migration." The second half does not exist. Grepping the whole scripts/ tree, fingerprintDetect is imported and called in exactly one place, scripts/migrate/migrate.mjs:354, inside step 1 (detect current version), and only when the meta row is absent or names an unknown version. After runPlan returns, migrate.mjs goes straight from the failure check at line 543 to writeMeta at line 550 with no re-read of the live schema and no comparison against getVersion(target).fingerprint. getActualSchema is likewise only called at line 353.
impact: There is no gate between "every SQL statement executed without error" and "the schema now matches version X". That is the structural reason migrate-01 could regress by 11 tables while db:migrate kept reporting success, and it is why the same class of defect has now shipped twice (AUDIT-009#migration-01, then again). It also means a version file that is simply incomplete, or a step whose IF NOT EXISTS silently no-ops against a pre-existing object of the same name (see migrate-06), produces an identical success message.
recommendation: Add a verification step to migrate.mjs between runPlan and writeMeta: re-run getActualSchema, compare against getVersion(target).fingerprint's tables and columns, and refuse to write the meta row (exit non-zero, naming every missing table and column) if anything is absent. Combined with migrate-10's parity test, that gives one guard at author time and one at run time.

title: The only migration test suite asserts against hardcoded name lists with arrayContaining, so it structurally cannot detect drift from instrumentation.ts
category: test cannot fail for the defect it appears to guard
description: tests/scripts/migrate/versions/2.0.0-to-3.0.0.test.ts is the only test that touches scripts/migrate/versions/. Its central assertion, "upgrade adds every table that survives to the final v3.0.0 shape" (line 30), is `expect(names).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([...literal list...]))`. arrayContaining is a subset check, and the literal list is maintained by hand in the test file, so the test passes as long as the migration contains the names someone remembered to type. It never reads instrumentation.ts, never enumerates its CREATE TABLE statements, and never compares the two sets in either direction. The sibling assertions at lines 139, 175, 187, 195, 233, 279, 306 and the fingerprint assertions at 370-476 all have the same shape. The list at line 30 even carries a comment naming the four tables AUDIT-009#migration-01 caught, which is a record of the defect but not a guard against it.
impact: Every one of the 11 tables and 8 columns in migrate-01 was added to instrumentation.ts while this suite stayed green. The project has now had the same drift twice, and the test that exists specifically because of the first occurrence cannot fail for the second. Because scripts/** is excluded from coverage in vitest.config.ts, coverage reporting also does not surface the gap.
recommendation: Add one parity test that parses instrumentation.ts for `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS <name>` and `ALTER TABLE <t> ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS <c>` (the same regex scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs:227 already uses to extract those blocks), builds the same set from the v1 baseline plus every version file's addTables/addColumns, and asserts set equality with toEqual, not arrayContaining. Assert the fingerprint in _registry.mjs equals the same set. An explicit allowlist constant can carry any deliberate exception, so adding one is a conscious edit rather than a silent omission.

title: Boot-time schema application takes no advisory lock, so two instances starting together race on CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and one exits 1
description: register() issues its schema statements as 94 separate pool.query calls with no BEGIN, no COMMIT and no lock of any kind; grepping instrumentation.ts for pg_advisory_lock, BEGIN or CONCURRENTLY returns nothing. PostgreSQL's IF NOT EXISTS is a catalog existence check followed by an insert, not an atomic operation, so two backends running the same CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS concurrently can both pass the check and one gets `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "pg_type_typname_nsp_index"` (23505) or `relation already exists` (42P07); the same race on CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS raises 23505 on pg_class, and concurrent ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS raises `tuple concurrently updated`. 41 of those pool.query calls carry no .catch, including the entire core-table run from line 279 (users) through line 1167 (subdomain_cache). An error in any of them unwinds to the outer catch at line 3618, which sends a critical admin alert and calls process.exit(1).
impact: Any deployment that starts more than one Node process against the same database (a scale-up, a rolling restart, docker compose with a replica, or a supervisor restarting a crashed process while the old one is still initializing) can lose one instance to a schema race on startup. The failure is transient (the next attempt sees the object already present) but it presents as a critical boot_schema_creation_failed alert and a crash-looping container, which is indistinguishable from a genuine schema problem. The 53 blocks that do have a .catch degrade differently and worse: they log non-fatally and let the app serve traffic on a schema whose creation actually failed.
recommendation: Wrap the whole schema block in a session-level `SELECT pg_advisory_lock(<constant>)` taken on a dedicated client before the first CREATE TABLE and released in a finally, so a second booting instance blocks until the first finishes and then finds every object present. Take the lock on a single pool.connect() client, not on the pool, so it is held for the duration.

title: The pre-migration backup passes the database password in pg_dump's argv and writes an unencrypted, never-pruned dump, both of which backup-db.mjs was explicitly fixed to avoid
category: two backup implementations with different security properties
description: backupDatabase, called from scripts/migrate/migrate.mjs:519 before any DDL runs, spawns `pg_dump [connectionString]` with the full DATABASE_URL as argv[1]. scripts/backup-db.mjs:214-221 does the opposite and documents why: "Keep the DB password out of pg_dump's argv (visible via ps on a shared host); libpq reads it from PGPASSWORD in the child env instead", using splitDbUrlForEnv from scripts/_lib/_lib.db-url.mjs. The migration-time copy imports neither. The same file writes the dump to databases/v{major}/{version}/vulnradar_backup_{ts}.sql (line 59) as plaintext SQL with no encryption, while backup-db.mjs:194-197 encrypts with AES-256-GCM by default and falls back to API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY specifically so backups are "encrypted by default rather than silently written in plaintext". There is also no retention pruning on this path, unlike backup-db.mjs's selectExpiredBackups.
impact: db:migrate is run on the production host, including automatically as the self-updater's last step, so on any shared or multi-tenant host the production database password is briefly readable in the process list by every local user. The dump it writes contains every password hash, every encrypted API key and token, every Stripe customer and subscription id, and the full scan history, sitting unencrypted under the app directory and accumulating one file per migration forever. On the self-hosted panel deployments the docs target, that directory is typically browsable through the panel's file manager.
recommendation: In scripts/_lib/_lib.backup.mjs, import splitDbUrlForEnv from ./_lib.db-url.mjs and spawn pg_dump with `[connArg]` plus the returned env, exactly as scripts/backup-db.mjs:216 does. Then reuse backup-db.mjs's createBackupCipher and selectExpiredBackups here rather than maintaining a second, weaker dump path, or have backupDatabase simply invoke runBackup with a version-scoped --dir.

title: Every index is built without CONCURRENTLY and the migration rewrites scan_history twice inside one transaction, while the self-updater runs it against a still-serving app
description: runPlan wraps the entire plan in a single BEGIN/COMMIT (line 95 to line 134) because "half-migrated schemas are the worst-case outcome", and the file header notes CONCURRENTLY is deliberately avoided since it cannot run in a transaction. The 2.0.0 to 3.0.0 plan contains 18 CREATE TABLE, 48 ADD COLUMN, 17 CREATE INDEX and 18 dataUpdates, all under that one transaction. Two of the ADD COLUMNs force a full rewrite of scan_history and hold ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on it for the whole remaining transaction: `share_token_hash TEXT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED` (2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs:608-615) and `public_id TEXT DEFAULT (replace(gen_random_uuid()::text, '-', ''))` (line 879-883), whose volatile default is evaluated once per existing row. A third, `UPDATE scan_history SET public_id = ... WHERE public_id IS NULL` (line 1059), is an unbounded UPDATE over the same table. The boot path has the same property without the transaction: all 103 CREATE INDEX / CREATE UNIQUE INDEX statements in instrumentation.ts are plain, taking a SHARE lock that blocks writes for the build, and the same two scan_history rewrites appear at instrumentation.ts:1284 and 2613. The self-updater runs db:migrate from inside the running app and explicitly does not restart it (app/api/v3/admin/updater/apply/route.ts:28), so the app is serving throughout.
impact: At the current production size (roughly 50 users) this is seconds, not minutes, so the practical cost today is a short stall rather than an outage. But every request that reads or writes scan_history or users blocks for the full duration of the migration transaction, with no timeout and no warning anywhere in the UI: the updater dialog tells the operator only that the server is not restarted, implying it keeps serving normally. The cost scales linearly with scan_history, which is the fastest-growing table in the product, so the same release flow gets worse every month with no signal until it is a real outage.
recommendation: Split the plan into a transactional DDL phase and a post-commit index phase, and run the CREATE INDEX steps outside the transaction with CONCURRENTLY (which requires per-statement error handling and a re-run path for INVALID indexes). Set `SET LOCAL lock_timeout` and `statement_timeout` at the start of the migration transaction so a blocked ACCESS EXCLUSIVE acquisition fails fast instead of queuing every request behind it. Add a warning to the updater dialog that db:migrate briefly locks the database.

title: access_rules.created_by carries two conflicting foreign keys because the self-healing migration adds ON DELETE SET NULL but never drops the original inline NO ACTION constraint
description: The CREATE TABLE for access_rules declares `created_by INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id)` (instrumentation.ts:1014, and identically in scripts/migrate/versions/_snippets.mjs:27). An inline REFERENCES with no ON DELETE clause creates a real, named constraint, `access_rules_created_by_fkey`, with ON DELETE NO ACTION. The self-healing block at instrumentation.ts:1033-1062 then checks only for a constraint named `fk_access_rules_created_by`; when absent it runs `ALTER TABLE access_rules ALTER COLUMN created_by DROP NOT NULL` (:1044) followed by `ADD CONSTRAINT fk_access_rules_created_by FOREIGN KEY (created_by) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` (:1047). It never drops `access_rules_created_by_fkey`, so the column ends up with two foreign keys to the same parent with contradictory delete actions. Compare the sibling fix 1,840 lines later for the identical bug class on broadcast_messages.created_by, which explicitly runs `DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS broadcast_messages_created_by_fkey` (instrumentation.ts:2895) before adding the SET NULL version, and the admin_audit_log.target_user_id fix at :592-622, which sidesteps the problem by declaring the column as plain `INTEGER` with no inline REFERENCES (:571). access_rules is the only one of the three that leaves the original constraint in place. On top of that, lib/auth/account-deletion.ts explicitly nulls the four other plain-FK columns it knows about (security_alerts.resolved_by :155, system_settings.updated_by :159, broadcast_messages.sent_by :167, sessions.impersonated_by :174) and does not null access_rules.created_by, because it assumes the schema-level SET NULL handles it. On `DELETE FROM users WHERE id = $1` (account-deletion.ts:180) Postgres queues one after-row RI trigger per constraint and fires them in trigger-name order, which for internal RI triggers is constraint-OID order, so the older NO ACTION check on `access_rules_created_by_fkey` runs before the newer SET NULL action and sees the still-referencing row. Note that the existing account-deletion test suite cannot catch this: tests/lib/auth/account-deletion.test.ts drives the function with a fake client, so no real constraint is ever evaluated.
impact: Any staff account that ever created an IP or URL access rule from the admin panel cannot be deleted. Both delete paths (POST /api/v3/account/delete and the admin delete_account action at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:2000) wrap deleteUserAccountData in one transaction, so the foreign-key violation rolls the whole thing back and the user gets a 500 on a GDPR erasure request. This is exactly the failure AUDIT-001#db-01 reported for admin_audit_log and this block was written to prevent. Even in the benign ordering where the delete succeeds, every INSERT and UPDATE on access_rules pays two identical RI checks instead of one, and any future reader of the schema sees two constraints disagreeing about what a user deletion means.
recommendation: In instrumentation.ts's access_rules self-healing block (around line 1041), add `ALTER TABLE access_rules DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS access_rules_created_by_fkey;` before the ADD CONSTRAINT, matching the broadcast_messages fix at :2895. Also drop the inline `REFERENCES users(id)` from the CREATE TABLE at :1014 and from scripts/migrate/versions/_snippets.mjs:27 so a fresh install never creates the NO ACTION constraint in the first place. To confirm the current state on a live database: `SELECT conname, confdeltype FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'access_rules'::regclass AND contype = 'f';` should return one row, not two.

title: Two tables exist only as lazy runtime DDL: staff_invites and admin_audit_log_archive are in no schema file, no migration, and no required-table check, and staff_invites re-runs its CREATE TABLE on every admin request
description: instrumentation.ts is documented as the canonical schema and contains 64 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements. Two more tables exist that it never creates. (1) `staff_invites` is created by `ensureStaffInvitesTable()` (lib/admin/staff-invites.ts:33-48), whose own doc comment at :22-31 says it is "intentionally NOT called from instrumentation.ts directly" and instructs whoever wires the schema change to add the import there. That was never done: a repo-wide grep for `ensureStaffInvitesTable` finds it called only from the three handlers in app/api/v3/admin/staff-invites/route.ts (:75, :177, :216), never at boot. (2) `admin_audit_log_archive` is created by `ensureAuditLogArchiveTable()` (lib/database/audit-log-archive.ts:43-57), whose doc comment at :37-41 gives the same never-executed wiring instruction; the only real call site is inside `archiveAdminAuditLogBeforePurge` at :77, which runs it against the transactional client of the nightly cleanup pass (lib/database/cleanup.ts:308), so DDL executes inside the long cleanup transaction on every run. Neither table appears anywhere in scripts/create-fresh-db/ or scripts/migrate/ (grep for both names in those directories returns nothing), and neither is in lib/database/required-tables.ts, so the boot-time verification at instrumentation.ts:3515-3543 and GET /api/v3/health both report a healthy schema on a database that is missing them. The public accept endpoint app/api/v3/auth/staff-invite/[token]/route.ts queries `staff_invites` at :57, :104 and :208 without ever calling ensureStaffInvitesTable first.
impact: `npm run db:create` and `npm run db:migrate` both produce a database that is missing these two tables, and nothing reports it. The staff-invite feature only works because its admin route happens to create the table as a side effect of the first request. That side effect also means every GET, POST and DELETE on /api/v3/admin/staff-invites executes one CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plus two CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS against the system catalogs before doing any work, which is the same per-request DDL antipattern AUDIT-003#misc-01 reported for ai/conversations and that was fixed there. Anyone reading instrumentation.ts to understand the schema, or diffing it against a production database, gets a wrong answer for two tables.
recommendation: Move both CREATE TABLE statements into instrumentation.ts's boot block, as each module's own doc comment already asks: put staff_invites next to team_invites (after line 917) and admin_audit_log_archive next to admin_audit_log (after line 579). Keep the ensure* functions but call them once at boot and delete the calls from app/api/v3/admin/staff-invites/route.ts:75, :177 and :216 and from lib/database/audit-log-archive.ts:77 so no DDL runs on a request path or inside the cleanup transaction. Add both names to lib/database/required-tables.ts, and add the DDL to scripts/create-fresh-db and the current migration version so a fresh install and a migrated install agree.

title: Twenty-six foreign-key child columns have no index, so every user deletion and every scan retention pass sequentially scans the child tables once per deleted parent row
description: Extends AUDIT-012#perf-15, which named nine missing indexes chosen from application WHERE/ORDER BY clauses. This is the orthogonal set: Postgres does not index a foreign-key child column automatically, and for every FK constraint it fires one referential-integrity query per deleted parent row (`DELETE FROM child WHERE fk = $1` for CASCADE, `UPDATE child SET fk = NULL WHERE fk = $1` for SET NULL). Cross-checking all 84 REFERENCES clauses in instrumentation.ts against all 97 CREATE INDEX statements leaves 26 FK columns with no index at all. Two of them hang off scan_history and are the worst: `scan_finding_feedback.scan_history_id` (instrumentation.ts:1460, ON DELETE SET NULL) and `auto_tag_dismissals.scan_id` (:2505, ON DELETE CASCADE). auto_tag_dismissals' only index is on `tag` (:2511) and scan_finding_feedback's three indexes are on (user_id, finding_id, finding_url), (finding_id, verdict) and (user_id, created_at) (:1467-1472), none of which lead with the scan column. Both fire on the four per-plan retention DELETEs in lib/database/cleanup.ts:152-195, which run inside the single 350-line cleanup transaction, and on `DELETE FROM scan_history WHERE user_id = $1` in lib/auth/account-deletion.ts:79. The scan_history sibling FKs are fine: scan_tags.scan_id is indexed (:446), scan_screenshots.scan_id is the primary key (:1378), and host_reputation.source_scan_id has a partial index whose predicate an equality lookup satisfies (:1723). Twenty-three more unindexed FK columns point at users(id) and each adds one sequential scan to `DELETE FROM users WHERE id = $1` (account-deletion.ts:180): sessions.impersonated_by (:347), user_badges.awarded_by (:510), admin_user_notes.admin_id (:698), password_reset_tokens.user_id (:753), email_verification_tokens.user_id (:763), teams.owner_id (:890), team_invites.invited_by (:911), gifted_subscriptions.gifted_by (:948) and .revoked_by (:953), admin_notifications.created_by (:985), access_rules.created_by (:1014), security_alerts.resolved_by (:1103), system_settings.updated_by (:1122), broadcast_messages.created_by (:1139) and .sent_by (:1330), auto_tag_dismissals.dismissed_by_user_id (:2507), promoted_auto_tag_rules.created_by (:2947), ai_credit_purchases.user_id (:2994), github_credit_purchases.user_id (:3026), browserbase_credit_purchases.user_id (:3096), support_ticket_messages.author_user_id (:3449), support_ticket_shares.shared_by_user_id (:3463), and staff_invites.invited_by (lib/admin/staff-invites.ts:40). The last of those, user_badges.badge_id (:508), points at badges. password_reset_tokens.user_id and email_verification_tokens.user_id are also hit outside deletion, by the explicit `DELETE FROM ... WHERE user_id = $1` that precedes every token issue (app/api/v3/auth/forgot-password/route.ts:81, app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:186, lib/auth/email-verification.ts:37, app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:787). Note that scripts/create-fresh-db/schemas/instrumentation-v1.ts:258 does create `idx_prt_user_id ON password_reset_tokens(user_id)`, so a database built from that older path has an index the current canonical schema never creates.
impact: Deleting one user runs about 23 sequential scans of unrelated tables, several of which (sessions, support_ticket_messages, gifted_subscriptions) grow without bound. More seriously, a nightly retention pass that deletes N free-plan scans performs N sequential scans of scan_finding_feedback and N of auto_tag_dismissals, all inside the single transaction AUDIT-012#perf-22 already flagged for holding a pooled connection for its whole duration. At today's row counts this is invisible; it degrades quadratically with scan volume, and the failure mode is the cleanup transaction holding locks for minutes and eventually timing out, which stops every retention rule at once because the whole pass is one transaction.
recommendation: Add the two scan_history child indexes first, since they are the ones that scale with scan volume: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_sff_scan_history_id ON scan_finding_feedback(scan_history_id) WHERE scan_history_id IS NOT NULL;` and `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_auto_tag_dismissals_scan_id ON auto_tag_dismissals(scan_id);` in the performance-index block at instrumentation.ts:1584. Then add plain indexes for password_reset_tokens(user_id), email_verification_tokens(user_id), sessions(impersonated_by), support_ticket_messages(author_user_id) and teams(owner_id). For the remaining low-traffic bookkeeping columns (created_by, revoked_by, updated_by, awarded_by, sent_by, dismissed_by_user_id) use partial indexes `WHERE col IS NOT NULL` so they stay small. Adding these is also the cheapest way to bound the cost of the transaction in lib/database/cleanup.ts.

title: No request or scan correlation id exists anywhere, and system_error_logs stores only a free-text message with no level, route, user, or scan column
description: The only structured error store is system_error_logs, created at instrumentation.ts:636-641 as `(id SERIAL, message TEXT, detail TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ)`. lib/database/error-log-capture.ts:169-173 inserts exactly `(message, detail)`, formed by string-joining whatever arguments a console.error call happened to pass. There is no level column (console.warn is not captured at all, only console.error at :137), no route, no user id, no scan id, and no request id. Nothing in the app generates a request id: no middleware.ts code sets or reads an x-request-id header, and the only `requestId` identifiers in the tree belong to unrelated features (app/api/v3/scan/discover/route.ts:96 for discovery progress, lib/browserbase/network-capture.ts:76 for CDP frames). GET /api/v3/admin/error-logs (app/api/v3/admin/error-logs/route.ts:37) can therefore only offer page/limit/free-text search over message and detail. The gap is visible in the product copy: components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:129 tells the user "The error is logged with the reference below" and no reference is ever rendered, because DashboardErrorState has no id prop at all (:22-33).
impact: When a user reports "my scan failed around 3pm", an operator cannot filter to that user or that scan. They grep free-form English across every console.error the process made, from 328 call sites, with a coalescing window and a 100-insert-per-minute cap (error-log-capture.ts:73-79) that can drop exactly the burst they are looking for. Any multi-hop failure (route -> executeScan -> a check -> safeFetch) produces several unrelated-looking rows with nothing tying them together.
recommendation: Add `level`, `route`, `user_id`, `scan_id` and `request_id` columns to system_error_logs in instrumentation.ts and populate them from an AsyncLocalStorage context set in middleware.ts (generate a request id there, echo it as x-request-id). Have lib/database/error-log-capture.ts read that context in the wrapper at :137. Thread scanId into the scanner's console.error calls. Then surface the id in components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx so the sentence at :129 is true.

title: The scan progress tracker writes two UPDATEs to scan_history per category, so a single scan does about 40 row rewrites of the widest table in the schema
description: `createProgressTracker`'s `onProgress` hook fires an `UPDATE scan_history SET current_category = $1, categories_total = $2 WHERE id = $3` on every "start" event (lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:120-127) and an `UPDATE scan_history SET categories_completed = $1, categories_total = $2 ...` on every "done" event (lines 131-138). The hook is invoked twice per category by `runSyncChecks` (lib/scanner/engine.ts:166 and :203) and twice per branch by `runAsyncChecksDetailed` (lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:4642 and :4644). `categoriesTotal` is `plannedSync.length + plannedAsync.length` (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:339), which for a default full scan is roughly 16 sync categories plus 4-5 async branches -- about 40 UPDATEs per scan. Because Postgres is MVCC, each one writes a new version of a `scan_history` row that carries the `findings`, `summary`, `response_headers` and `result_meta` JSONB columns.
impact: About 40 dead tuples per scan on the largest table in the schema, plus 40 write round trips competing for the same 10-connection pool the scan's own reads use. On a crawl this is 40 x page count. It also inflates autovacuum work on the one table every list, dashboard and public page reads from.
recommendation: Coalesce progress writes in lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:113: keep the counters in memory and flush at most once every ~500ms (or only when `current_category` actually changes) with a single UPDATE, dropping the separate start/done writes. The status poll already runs on a 2s interval (AUDIT-011 scan-03), so sub-second progress precision buys nothing.

title: Nine missing indexes: four force full table scans inside the single long cleanup transaction, two make per-scan triage lookups degrade with total history
description: Cross-checking every index in instrumentation.ts against the WHERE/JOIN/ORDER BY columns in app/ and lib/ leaves these gaps. (1) `rate_limits.window_start` has no index -- `UNIQUE(key, window_start)` (instrumentation.ts:842) leads on `key` -- so `DELETE FROM rate_limits WHERE window_start < NOW() - INTERVAL '1 day'` (lib/database/cleanup.ts:211) seq-scans the fastest-growing table in the schema. (2)(3)(4) The same shape on `scan_finding_feedback.created_at` (cleanup.ts:380), `user_notifications.created_at` (cleanup.ts:389) and `github_review_usage.updated_at` (cleanup.ts:401): each table's only timestamp index is a composite led by `user_id` (instrumentation.ts:1471, 1672, 2047), unusable as a timestamp-only scan key -- while admin_audit_log, email_logs, system_error_logs and api_usage all do have the plain index their identical prune uses. (5) `ai_conversations.last_message_at` has no index; the table has `idx_ai_conversations_created_at` (instrumentation.ts:1191) on the wrong column, and both real consumers use `last_message_at` (cleanup.ts:353 and app/api/v3/ai/conversations/route.ts:171-175, which also sorts by it). (6)(7) `finding_remediation(user_id, finding_url)` and `scan_finding_feedback(user_id, finding_url)`: both tables have `UNIQUE (user_id, finding_id, finding_url)` (instrumentation.ts:1516, 1467), with `finding_id` sitting between the two columns the hot queries actually filter on (lib/scanner/remediation-store.ts:41-44, lib/scanner/regression-alert.ts:47-49), so only `user_id` is usable as a key. (8) `broadcast_recipients(message_id, user_id)` -- see perf-07. (9) the public-shares partial index -- see perf-04.
impact: The cleanup pass (lib/database/cleanup.ts) performs four full table scans on the largest, fastest-growing tables, all inside one transaction (see perf-22). `getRemediationMap` runs on every scan-result render and `regression-alert` after every completed scan; both currently cost O(that user's entire triage history) instead of O(findings for this URL), so a heavy user's scans get slower the more findings they have ever triaged. The admin AI-conversations page seq-scans and externally sorts a table of JSONB message arrays on every load.
recommendation: Add to the performance-index block in instrumentation.ts (around line 1587): `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_rate_limits_window_start ON rate_limits(window_start); CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_ai_conversations_last_msg ON ai_conversations(last_message_at DESC); CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_user_notifications_created ON user_notifications(created_at); CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_sff_created ON scan_finding_feedback(created_at); CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_gru_updated ON github_review_usage(updated_at); CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_finding_remediation_user_url ON finding_remediation(user_id, finding_url); CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_sff_user_url ON scan_finding_feedback(user_id, finding_url);` Keep the existing three-column UNIQUEs -- they back the `ON CONFLICT` clauses in app/api/v3/scan/remediation/route.ts:93 and app/api/v3/scan/feedback/route.ts:60. `idx_ai_conversations_created_at` has no reader and can be dropped.

title: Four hot queries wrap an indexed column in a function or regex, so the index that exists for them can never be used
description: (a) app/api/v3/host/[hostname]/trend/route.ts:77-82 filters `WHERE is_public = true AND status = 'completed' AND url ~* $1`, with `$1` built as `^https?://(www\.)?<host>([:/?]|$)` at line 70. `~*` is not a b-tree-indexable operator, so `idx_scan_history_url_public_completed` (instrumentation.ts:2359) degrades to a full scan applying a case-insensitive regex to every row, then a sort, and only then `LIMIT 30`. The query also selects the full `findings` JSONB for those 30 rows. This is a public unauthenticated page. (b) app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:75 joins on `DATE(sh.scanned_at) = days.day` (see perf-06). (c) lib/domains/scope.ts:47-53 filters `($1 = domain OR $1 LIKE '%.' || domain)` -- the LIKE pattern is built from the column with the parameter on the left, which no b-tree can serve, so `idx_domains_domain_verified` (instrumentation.ts:3189) is unusable and every scan authorization check scans all verified domains across all tenants. (d) app/api/v3/admin/blocked-data/route.ts:60-83 and its DELETE twin at :124-135 apply `LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(sh.url, ...))` per row over all of scan_history before the `LIMIT 100`.
impact: Each of these reads the whole table where an index exists specifically to prevent that. (a) and (c) are the ones that matter operationally: (a) is on an unauthenticated route whose cost grows with total public scan volume, and (c) runs on the authorization gate for every active-probe or port-scan request.
recommendation: For (a), store the normalized host at scan time (a `host` column populated from lib/scanner/root-domain.ts, indexed) and filter `WHERE host = $1` instead of regexing the URL; also stop selecting `findings` there and project only title/severity. For (b), rewrite as a range predicate. For (c), store the registrable domain and each of its parent suffixes so the lookup becomes `domain = ANY($1::text[])`, which is indexable. For (d), the same normalized `host` column removes the REGEXP_REPLACE.

title: The nightly cleanup runs about thirty DELETEs, four of them full table scans, inside one 350-line transaction holding a pooled connection
description: `lib/database/cleanup.ts` opens `BEGIN` at line 114 and does not `COMMIT` until line 464, wrapping roughly thirty DELETE statements across sessions, rate_limits, tokens, scan_history, scan_finding_feedback, user_notifications, github_review_usage, ai_conversations and more in a single transaction on one pooled client. Four of those DELETEs cannot use an index and seq-scan their table (see perf-15): rate_limits (line 211), scan_finding_feedback (line 380), user_notifications (line 389), github_review_usage (line 401). None of the work is transactionally coupled -- these are independent retention prunes on unrelated tables.
impact: One of the 10 pool connections is held for the entire pass, and every row deleted stays locked for its duration, so any concurrent write touching those rows blocks. The four full scans make the pass length grow with total table size rather than with the number of rows actually being deleted. A failure at line 480 rolls back thirty prunes that had nothing to do with each other.
recommendation: Split the pass in lib/database/cleanup.ts:114-464 into one autocommitted statement per table (or small groups), with the batching pattern `DELETE ... WHERE ctid IN (SELECT ctid ... LIMIT 5000)` in a loop for the large tables, so no single statement holds locks for long. Add the four missing indexes from perf-15 first.

title: Auth pages prerender a null Suspense fallback, so first paint is empty and the indexable /login is one empty div
description: app/reset-password/page.tsx:41 uses Suspense fallback={null}, prerendered into the static HTML, while the pitch column is hidden lg:block. First paint on a phone is wordmark, empty band, footer. The same shape at app/login/page.tsx:12 and app/signup/page.tsx:12 replaces the entire page.
impact: A blank first paint on the three highest-intent pages in the product, and the HTML a crawler receives for the indexable /login is a single empty div.
recommendation: Give each Suspense a real skeleton fallback.

title: Twelve schema columns are written and never read, or defined and never written
description: Verified dead, each with the grep that found no live reference: users.beta_access (:303) hardcoded false in every INSERT (lib/auth/auth.ts:282,361,382; staff-invite/[token]/route.ts:199), no UPDATE, no gate; users.email_session_revoked (:317) a legacy duplicate whose nine live references all resolve to notification_preferences; users.daily_scan_limit (:304) see drift-05; broadcast_recipients.opened_at and .clicked_at (:1155-1156) DDL only; broadcast_messages.scheduled_at (:1137) inserted but no worker consumes it and status is hardcoded 'draft' then 'sent', so the CHECK values 'scheduled' and 'cancelled' are unwritable; broadcast_messages.message_type (:1135) hardcoded "email" by the UI and never read by the send path (:504); data_requests.completed_at (:876) DDL only, the route uses downloaded_at; system_settings.setting_type (:1121) DDL only; gifted_subscriptions.reason (:950) selected in the GDPR export but the only INSERT (admin/route.ts:1671) omits it and the gift dialog has no field; badges.is_limited (:496) only ever inserted as false with no UPDATE anywhere; api_keys.team_id (:931) no reference in lib/api/api-keys.ts or app/api/v3/keys; scan_screenshots.width and .height (:1381-1382) written at lib/scanner/page-screenshot.ts:295, never selected, consumers read the result_meta copy.
impact: Schema noise that misleads anyone reading the model, plus three cases (beta_access, message_type, scheduled_at) that look like shipped features and are not.
recommendation: Decide per column: wire it or drop it. Deletions need owner sign-off. beta_access, broadcast scheduling and broadcast message_type are the three worth a product decision rather than a silent drop.

title: Schema-creation failure during boot is swallowed, letting the app serve traffic against a partially-initialized database
description: instrumentation.ts wraps its entire ~30-table CREATE TABLE sequence (users, sessions, scan_history, billing_history, webhooks, etc.) in one try/catch that, on failure, only console.errors 'Database migration failed' and lets the process continue starting -- unlike the schema-version check just above it, which correctly process.exit(1)s on a mismatch. A transient DB hiccup partway through this sequence (e.g. a connection drop while creating the 15th of 30 tables) leaves some tables missing while the app still comes up and starts accepting requests. The readiness endpoint (/api/v3/health) only verifies pool connectivity and the vulnradar_schema_meta version row, not that every application table actually exists, so it would report 'ok' while requests touching the missing table 500 repeatedly. Evidence: instrumentation.ts line 257 (try open) through line 2978 (`catch (error) { console.error(...); }` with no process.exit), contrasted with the schema-version mismatch check at lines 143-178 which does process.exit(1); app/api/v3/health/route.ts's probeDatabase only SELECTs from vulnradar_schema_meta and never checks for the presence of other tables.
recommendation: NOT YET APPLIED -- reported for review. Recommendation: Either re-throw/process.exit after logging in that outer catch (matching the schema-version check's behavior), or have the health endpoint additionally verify a canonical set of critical tables exist before reporting 'ok'.

title: Dead revokeApiKey/getUserApiKeys duplicate in db-utils.ts is missing the ownership check the live version has
description: lib/database/db-utils.ts duplicates getUserApiKeys/revokeApiKey from lib/api/api-keys.ts. The db-utils.ts revokeApiKey(keyId) takes no userId and updates WHERE id = $1 only (an IDOR shape) vs. api-keys.ts's WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2. Confirmed dead code: db-utils.ts is imported exactly once anywhere, only for getUserByEmail, so the unsafe revokeApiKey is never actually called, but it's a landmine for the next person who greps for revokeApiKey and finds two candidates.
recommendation: Delete the db-utils.ts duplicates; keep lib/api/api-keys.ts as the sole implementation.

title: repairAllSequences() runs unguarded immediately after COMMIT; a failure there masks a successful migration as a reported failure
description: In scripts/migrate/_runner.mjs's runPlan, await repairAllSequences(client) runs right after COMMIT with no try/catch. migrate.mjs only calls writeMeta() after runPlan() returns normally, so an exception here propagates past writeMeta -- every DDL step is already durably committed, but vulnradar_schema_meta is never updated, so the app refuses to boot and the operator sees a false 'Migration failed' for a migration that actually succeeded. The identical unguarded call exists in migrate.mjs's zero-step 'same version' branch. A second db:migrate run does safely re-converge since every DDL step is idempotent, but only after a confusing false failure. Verified via code reading; not reproduced live.
recommendation: Wrap the post-COMMIT repairAllSequences(client) call in runPlan, and the analogous call in migrate.mjs's zero-step branch, in their own try/catch that logs a warning without letting the exception mask a successful migration or block the meta-row write.

title: Webhook HMAC signing secret is stored in plaintext, unlike every other reversible secret in the codebase
description: POST /api/v3/webhooks generates a 256-bit secret and inserts it directly into webhooks.secret, a plain TEXT column. Neither the webhooks route nor lib/webhooks/delivery.ts calls encryptApiKey/decryptApiKey. Every other long-lived secret the app needs back in plaintext for repeated use (API keys, TOTP seeds, Discord OAuth tokens) goes through lib/auth/crypto.ts's AES-256-GCM encryptApiKey/decryptApiKey. A DB-level compromise lets an attacker read every user's webhook secret and forge validly-signed payloads to their receivers.
recommendation: Encrypt webhooks.secret at rest with the existing encryptApiKey/decryptApiKey helpers, decrypting only where signWebhookPayload needs the raw secret. Backfill existing plaintext rows in a migration.

title: account/delete blocked by FK violation on admin_audit_log
description: admin_audit_log.target_user_id and access_rules.created_by had no ON DELETE clause; user self-delete returned 500.
recommendation: Self-healing idempotent migration adds fk_admin_audit_target_user ON DELETE SET NULL and fk_access_rules_created_by ON DELETE SET NULL on startup.

title: /admin is served noindex on the stated grounds of saving crawl budget, but it is missing from DISALLOWED_PATHS so robots.txt still invites crawlers to fetch it
description: app/admin/layout.tsx:7 sets privatePageMetadata("Admin", "/admin") and its comment says "Keeping it out of the index also saves crawl budget for the public pages that can actually rank." But lib/seo/routes.ts:107 DISALLOWED_PATHS lists /dashboard, /profile, /compare, /history, /assets, /attack-surface, /repos, /shares, /shared/, /host/, /teams, /checkout, /browser/, /badge, /verify-email, /reset-password, /forgot-password and /unsubscribe, and not /admin. app/robots.ts:60 spreads that list, so the published robots.txt permits /admin and /admin/ai-chats/<id>. The meta tag still keeps both out of the index, so this is a crawl-budget gap rather than an exposure: an anonymous fetch of /admin is bounced to /login by middleware.ts:337 and shows nothing.
impact: Crawlers spend fetches on an admin route that redirects, and each redirect lands on /login?redirect=/admin, which is the exact query-parameter duplicate shape the QUERY_DISALLOW rule at app/robots.ts:52 was added to stop after Search Console flagged it.
