Small, but it is the one hole in an otherwise complete list, and the file's own comment claims the opposite.
recommendation: Add `"/admin",` to DISALLOWED_PATHS in lib/seo/routes.ts:107 next to /dashboard. Prefix matching covers /admin/ai-chats/<id> automatically, the same way /teams covers /teams/join and /checkout covers /checkout/success. While there, add a test that asserts every route whose metadata comes from privatePageMetadata has a matching DISALLOWED_PATHS prefix, which would have caught this and would catch the next one.

title: The indexed check count disagrees across two adjacent marketing surfaces: the landing meta description says "795+ deterministic checks" while the /checks meta description says "the full list of 749 security checks"
description: lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts:8 sets GENERATED_CHECKS_LABEL to "795+", derived from EXACT_CHECK_COUNT = 797 (line 6), which is EXACT_LEGACY_CHECK_COUNT 754 plus EXACT_PAGE_CHECK_COUNT 43. app/landing/page.tsx:32 uses that label verbatim in the landing meta description: "795+ deterministic checks across headers, TLS, cookies, DNS, and secrets". app/checks/page.tsx:26 computes `TOTAL = getAllChecks().length`, which is 754 minus the 5 entries filtered as "(disabled duplicate)" at lib/seo/checks-content.ts:129, giving 749, and line 29 puts that in the /checks meta description: "The full list of 749 security checks VulnRadar runs against a URL". Both numbers are internally defensible (795 counts the 43 PageCheck-architecture detectors that deliberately have no public page, per the comment at lib/seo/checks-content.ts:12-14) and neither is a lie, but they appear in two indexed snippets one click apart and differ by 46.
impact: A visitor who clicks a result promising 795+ checks lands on a page whose own first sentence says 749, which reads as a marketing exaggeration caught in the act. On a product whose entire pitch is deterministic, auditable detection, an unexplained number mismatch on the two highest-traffic public pages is a credibility cost out of proportion to the size of the bug.
recommendation: Make /checks state both numbers so they reconcile rather than contradict. Change app/checks/page.tsx:29 to something like `The ${TOTAL} security checks with a public fix guide, out of ${TOTAL_CHECKS_LABEL} VulnRadar runs, grouped into 18 categories.` and add one sentence to the page body explaining that the remaining detectors run inside multi-page analysis and have no standalone page. Update the first FAQ answer at app/checks/page.tsx:43, which currently says "documents 749 checks", to the same framing so the FAQPage structured data matches.

title: scripts/migrate/versions/_legacy-original.mjs is 871 lines of unreachable migration code whose only import resolves to a file that does not exist, so it crashes immediately if anyone runs it
category: archived dead script with a broken import
description: scripts/migrate/versions/_legacy-original.mjs is 871 lines, described by scripts/README.md:31 as 'Archived pre-refactor migrate.mjs'. Line 23-47 imports 22 named symbols (c, log, info, success, warn, error, banner, section, loadEnv, askYesNo, askDanger, getProjectMeta, createPool, connect, confirmIntro, requireDatabaseUrl, parseDbUrl, formatDbTarget, formatDbHost, buildConnectionString, chooseDatabase, ROOT) 'from "./_lib.mjs"'. Relative to scripts/migrate/versions/ that resolves to scripts/migrate/versions/_lib.mjs, which does not exist: the directory contains only 1.0.0-to-2.0.0.mjs, 2.0.0-to-1.0.0.mjs, 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs, _legacy-original.mjs and _snippets.mjs. The real helper lives at scripts/_lib/_lib.mjs, two directories up. The migration runner never loads it: listVersionFiles at scripts/migrate/_registry.mjs:633-636 filters out every filename starting with '_', and findVersionFile at :613-614 only resolves '<a>-to-<b>.mjs' names. Nothing else in the repo references it except that one README line. Nothing catches the broken import either, because eslint.config.mjs:32 ignores 'scripts/**' and tsconfig.json does not include .mjs at all. It is also unreachable by the runner: the only two ways a file in scripts/migrate/versions/ is loaded are findVersionFile (scripts/migrate/_registry.mjs:609), which builds candidate paths as `${from}-to-${to}.mjs` / `${to}-to-${from}.mjs` from registry version names, and listVersionFiles (scripts/migrate/_registry.mjs:633), which explicitly filters out every filename starting with an underscore. _legacy-original.mjs matches neither, and it has been dead since commit fb8a71de split the monolith. Verified during the merge: the file is 871 lines, scripts/migrate/versions/_lib.mjs does not exist, and the underscore filter is present as described.
impact: An operator following the README to 'the archived original migrator' as a fallback during a failed migration gets ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND instead of a working script, at the worst possible moment. Meanwhile 872 lines of stale v1/v2 schema knowledge sit next to the live migration steps, where a maintainer can copy an outdated DDL fragment out of it. Separately, 871 lines of stale v1/v2 schema knowledge sit in the directory the runner loads version files from, with its own private getActualSchema and version comparisons, so it reads as authoritative to the next maintainer looking for real migration behaviour and is a plausible place for someone to apply a fix that can never run.
recommendation: Delete scripts/migrate/versions/_legacy-original.mjs (872 lines) and the line describing it at scripts/README.md:31: git history is the archive. If it is genuinely wanted as a reference, at minimum fix line 47 to '../../_lib/_lib.mjs' and move it out of versions/ so it does not sit in the runner's scan directory.

title: Five CODEOWNERS rules match no path in the repository, including both database-migration rules, and scripts/README.md calls a script a CI gate that no workflow runs
description: .github/CODEOWNERS lists five path rules that cannot match anything in the current tree. Lines 17-19 name /app/api/v2/auth/, /app/api/v2/billing/ and /app/api/v2/webhooks/, but app/api/ contains only security-txt/, v3/ and version/: there is no v2. Lines 33-34 name /scripts/migrate.mjs and /scripts/create-fresh-db.mjs, both of which moved into subdirectories (scripts/migrate/migrate.mjs and scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs) and no longer exist at those paths. The header comment on those two calls them the 'Database migrations' owners. Separately, scripts/README.md:63 states 'The CI gate `node scripts/find-duplicate-ids.mjs` is also part of the pre-commit checklist'; no workflow under .github/workflows/ runs any script from scripts/ (the only references to scripts/ anywhere in .github/ are the two stale CODEOWNERS lines). Duplicate check ids are in fact gated, but by a vitest case at tests/lib/scanner/registry.test.ts:60 ('check IDs are unique across the registry'), not by that script.
impact: Low, because the catch-all '* @dbcaa @RejectModders' on CODEOWNERS line 10 already assigns both owners to every file, so no review is actually skipped. What is lost is intent: the five specific rules were written to mark security-critical and migration paths, and a future change to line 10 (say, adding a third owner or narrowing the catch-all) would silently leave the migration runner and the auth/billing/webhook API with no explicit owner. The README's 'CI gate' wording will make someone believe a check exists where it does not.
recommendation: In .github/CODEOWNERS replace lines 17-19 with /app/api/v3/auth/, /app/api/v3/billing/ and /app/api/v3/webhooks/, and lines 33-34 with /scripts/migrate/ and /scripts/create-fresh-db/. In scripts/README.md:63 either reword to 'pre-commit checklist (see AGENTS.md); duplicate ids are gated in CI by tests/lib/scanner/registry.test.ts', or add a step running node scripts/find-duplicate-ids.mjs to the lint job in .github/workflows/ci.yml so the sentence becomes true.

title: The github_review_usage year_month backfill gives every existing row the same window_start and then adds a UNIQUE constraint on it, aborting the whole migration on any table with two rows for one user
category: unique constraint added over a backfilled duplicate
description: The dataUpdates chain runs `ALTER TABLE github_review_usage ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS window_start TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` (line 1123), then drops year_month (line 1134), then `ADD CONSTRAINT github_review_usage_user_window_key UNIQUE (user_id, window_start)` (line 1151). NOW() is transaction-start time and is evaluated once, so every pre-existing row receives the identical window_start. The old shape was keyed by calendar month, so a user with rows for two different months collapses to two rows with the same (user_id, window_start) and the UNIQUE add fails with `could not create unique index ... Key is duplicated`. Because runPlan holds one transaction for the entire plan (_runner.mjs:95), that error rolls back the whole v2.0.0 to v3.0.0 upgrade, not just this step. instrumentation.ts:2015-2032 runs the identical statements at boot but inside a `.catch` that logs non-fatally, so there the table is left with no unique constraint at all and every subsequent `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id, window_start)` in lib/billing/github-review-usage.ts:168 fails with "there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification".
impact: This is the one place in the migration where a statement fails purely because of existing row values. Production has never had the year_month shape (production is on v2.3.x per the file header), so the blast radius today is developer and self-host databases that booted an intermediate build. On those, db:migrate aborts entirely with a duplicate-key error on a table nobody would think to look at, and app boot silently leaves GitHub AI review quota tracking broken.
recommendation: Replace the DEFAULT NOW() backfill with a deterministic per-row value derived from the old key, for example `ADD COLUMN window_start TIMESTAMPTZ` then `UPDATE github_review_usage SET window_start = to_timestamp(year_month || '-01', 'YYYY-MM-DD') WHERE window_start IS NULL`, then `SET NOT NULL`, so rows for different months stay distinct. Failing that, collapse duplicates first with a `DELETE ... USING` keeping MAX(tokens_used) per user before the ADD CONSTRAINT. Apply the same change to instrumentation.ts:2015 so the two paths agree.

title: The downgrade's red warning box never mentions that it deletes user accounts, and no documentation anywhere describes what to do when a migration fails
category: undisclosed destructive step and missing recovery procedure
description: showDowngradeWarning builds its "This will PERMANENTLY DELETE" list from `destructiveSteps.filter(s => s.kind === "dropTable")` and `... === "dropColumn"` (lines 227-228). Steps of kind "dataUpdate" are excluded from both filters and their dataLoss is always null (scripts/migrate/_planner.mjs:179-188), so the 3.0.0 to 2.0.0 downgrade's `DELETE FROM users WHERE password_hash IS NULL` (2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs:1293, destructive: true) never appears in the box the operator types yes-delete-data into. It also never appears in renderPlan's per-step "rows will be lost" detail (scripts/migrate/_planner.mjs:228-240), which likewise only handles kind table and column, so the only place the account deletion is stated is the `description` string in the source file, which is never printed. The same applies to the other silent losses that description names: pre_staff_plan and users.ai_credit_balance are dropped without being restored or refunded. Separately, grepping app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx, app/docs/setup/page.tsx and README.md for a failed-migration recovery procedure returns nothing: db:restore is mentioned only in README.md, and the pre-migration dump path (databases/v{major}/{version}/) is documented in no user-facing page at all.
impact: An operator running a downgrade sees a warning that names tables and columns and confirms with an exact phrase, believing that is the full extent of the data loss, while every OAuth-only account is deleted and every purchased AI credit balance is zeroed without either being named. And when a migration does fail, nothing tells the operator that a plaintext dump was just written to databases/, how to restore it, or that db:restore exists.
recommendation: In scripts/migrate/migrate.mjs's showDowngradeWarning, add a third section listing every step where `destructive === true && kind === "dataUpdate"`, printed with its label. Give the dataUpdates step shape an optional dataLoss field so 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs can declare what the DELETE removes, and render it in _planner.mjs's renderPlan. Add a "Recovering from a failed migration" section to app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx naming the databases/ dump location, npm run db:restore, and the fact that re-running db:migrate is safe.

title: The v1 to v2 downgrade definition is duplicated verbatim in two files and only one copy is ever loaded
description: Both scripts/migrate/versions/1.0.0-to-2.0.0.mjs:136-174 and scripts/migrate/versions/2.0.0-to-1.0.0.mjs:21-59 export a `downgrade` object containing the same 15 dropTables and the same 13 dropColumns, character for character. findVersionFile (scripts/migrate/_registry.mjs:612-615) tries `${from}-to-${to}.mjs` first, so a downgrade step of {from: "2.0.0", to: "1.0.0"} always resolves to 2.0.0-to-1.0.0.mjs and 1.0.0-to-2.0.0.mjs's downgrade export is never loaded by anything. 2.0.0-to-1.0.0.mjs's `upgrade` export (line 15-19) is symmetrically dead, since an upgrade step of {from: "1.0.0", to: "2.0.0"} resolves to the other file first. The brief for this audit is correct that a 2.0.0-to-1.0.0 downgrade file is deliberate; the duplication of its contents into the other file is the issue, not its existence.
impact: Someone fixing the v1 drop list has a 50 percent chance of editing the copy that never runs, and the two lists can silently diverge with the runtime behavior determined by filename ordering rather than by intent. They are identical today, so this is a latent hazard rather than a live bug.
recommendation: Pick one file as the home for the v1 to v2 pair. Either delete the dead `downgrade` from 1.0.0-to-2.0.0.mjs and keep 2.0.0-to-1.0.0.mjs as the down half, or delete 2.0.0-to-1.0.0.mjs entirely and rely on findVersionFile's documented reversed-name fallback, which already resolves 2.0.0 to 1.0.0 to 1.0.0-to-2.0.0.mjs's downgrade export. The second option matches how the 3.0.0 to 2.0.0 downgrade already works, since no 3.0.0-to-2.0.0.mjs exists.

title: Twenty-seven of the ninety-seven indexes are redundant: sixteen duplicate a UNIQUE constraint outright and eleven are strict prefixes of a wider index, and a code comment records the reasoning that created most of them
description: New relative to AUDIT-012#perf-15 and #perf-16, which covered missing and unusable indexes; this is the opposite direction. A UNIQUE constraint is implemented as a unique b-tree index, so a separate CREATE INDEX on the same column is a pure duplicate. Sixteen exist: idx_users_email (:323 vs :284), idx_users_stripe_customer (:326 vs :296), idx_api_keys_key_hash (:373 vs :362), idx_scan_history_share_token (:432 vs :425), idx_badges_name (:499 vs :490), idx_discord_user (:724 vs :711), idx_discord_id (:725 vs :712), idx_notif_prefs_user_id (:830 vs :802), idx_team_invites_token (:916 vs :910), idx_admin_notifications_cookie (:991 vs :966), idx_ai_conversations_session_id (:1192 vs :1184), idx_user_ai_configs_user_id (:1219 vs :1210), idx_github_connections_user (:1932 vs :1924), idx_github_review_usage_user_window (:2047 vs the UNIQUE added at :2034), idx_promoted_auto_tag_rules_tag (:2951 vs :2939), and idx_staff_invites_token (lib/admin/staff-invites.ts:45 vs :37). Eleven more are strict prefixes of a wider index or key, which a b-tree already serves: idx_scan_history_user_id (:430) under idx_scan_history_user_scanned (:1587), idx_api_usage_key_id (:408) under idx_api_usage_key_used (:1589), idx_admin_audit_admin_id (:577) under idx_admin_audit_admin_created (:1591), idx_scan_tags_scan_id (:446) under UNIQUE(scan_id, tag) (:444), idx_user_badges_user (:513) under PRIMARY KEY (user_id, badge_id) (:511), idx_rate_limits_key (:844) under UNIQUE(key, window_start) (:842), idx_device_trust_user_id (:863) under UNIQUE(user_id, device_fingerprint) (:861), idx_team_members_team (:902) under UNIQUE(team_id, user_id) (:900), idx_domains_user_id (:3187) under UNIQUE(user_id, domain) (:3185), idx_api_keys_key_locator_backfill (:376), a partial index whose rows are a subset of idx_api_keys_key_locator (:374), and idx_staff_activity_user_heartbeat (:743), a composite on (user_id, last_heartbeat) on a table with UNIQUE(user_id) (:741), which caps the table at one row per user so the second column can never narrow anything. The comment at :1571-1578 states the reasoning that produced the first three of the prefix cases: "The single-column indexes created above each table are left in place; these are additive, not replacements, so unrelated query shapes that only filter on one of the columns keep working the same way." A composite index leading with the same column already serves a filter on that column alone, so the premise is wrong. Separately, six indexes cover low-cardinality columns on tables that are tiny in this deployment (about 50 users) and will never be chosen by the planner over a sequential scan: idx_users_role (:324), idx_users_plan (:325), idx_admin_notifications_type (:990), idx_access_rules_type (:1023), idx_security_alerts_severity (:1108) and idx_broadcast_messages_status (:1143).
impact: Every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on these tables maintains a second copy of an index that can never be chosen, which is pure write amplification on the hottest tables in the schema: rate_limits (written on every rate-limited request), api_usage, scan_history and sessions. It also inflates the working set that has to stay in shared_buffers and doubles the vacuum work on those relations. The false comment at :1574 is a maintenance hazard on its own, because it will produce more duplicates the next time someone adds a composite index alongside an existing single-column one.
recommendation: Drop the 27 listed indexes with `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS`. Keep every UNIQUE constraint, they are the constraints doing the work. Fix the comment at instrumentation.ts:1571-1578 to say that a composite index leading with column A replaces a single-column index on A, and delete the three single-column indexes it was written to justify (:430, :408, :577). Verify against a live database with `SELECT indexrelid::regclass, indrelid::regclass, indkey FROM pg_index ORDER BY indrelid;` before dropping, since a self-hosted install created by an older path may have a slightly different set.

title: REQUIRED_TABLES lists 8 of the 66 tables the app creates and omits sessions, so a boot that fails to create the session table reports a healthy schema while every login 500s
description: REQUIRED_TABLES is `[users, scan_history, api_keys, host_reputation, host_badges, webhooks, scan_finding_feedback, system_error_logs]`. It is consumed by the boot-time verification at instrumentation.ts:3515-3543 (which fires a critical admin alert on a miss) and by GET /api/v3/health at app/api/v3/health/route.ts:110-116 (which reports missing_tables). Cross-checking it against the 64 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements in instrumentation.ts plus the two lazy ones from schema-02: every name in the list is genuinely created, so there is no phantom entry. The gap is the other direction. The file's own docstring says the list covers "auth, scanning, API keys, billing", and `sessions` is absent, even though lib/auth/auth.ts:99 reads it on every authenticated request and losing it takes down login, logout, and every dashboard route. Also absent and load-bearing: `rate_limits` (lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts:148, every rate-limited endpoint), `notification_preferences` (inserted on every signup at app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:200 and on every OAuth signup at oauth/[provider]/callback/route.ts:239), `processed_stripe_events` (the Stripe webhook idempotency guard at app/api/v3/webhooks/stripe/route.ts:168, whose own instrumentation.ts comment at :536-543 documents what happened the last time it was missing: every Stripe retry reprocessed as a new event), and the three payment idempotency ledgers ai_credit_purchases, github_credit_purchases and browserbase_credit_purchases, each of which is the sole guard against double-crediting a purchase (lib/billing/ai-usage.ts:160-172). Every one of those tables is created inside a `.catch()` that only console.errors, exactly the failure mode this list exists to catch.
impact: The health endpoint is the operator's only signal that the boot-time schema sequence half-completed. Today it can report schema_ok with no missing tables while sessions, rate_limits or processed_stripe_events do not exist, which means a monitor watching /api/v3/health stays green through an outage that makes login impossible or through a state where every Stripe webhook replay re-grants a plan.
recommendation: Add sessions, rate_limits, notification_preferences, processed_stripe_events, ai_credit_purchases, github_credit_purchases and browserbase_credit_purchases to REQUIRED_TABLES, plus staff_invites and admin_audit_log_archive once schema-02 is fixed. The docstring's argument against exhaustiveness (drift with instrumentation.ts) holds for a full 66-name list but not for the seven tables whose absence takes down auth, rate limiting, signup or billing idempotency.

title: The five most load-bearing enum columns (users.role, users.plan, team_members.role, domains.status, gifted_subscriptions.plan) have no CHECK constraint, while a dozen cosmetic ones do
description: CHECK coverage on enum-like text columns is inverted relative to importance. Constrained: admin_notifications.type/variant/audience (:969-971), access_rules.rule_type/value_type (:1007-1008), security_alerts.severity (:1097), broadcast_messages.message_type/status (:1135, :1141), broadcast_recipients.status (:1157), scan_finding_feedback.verdict (:1463), finding_remediation.status (:1506), scan_history.status (:1623), scan_tags.source (:2449), promoted_auto_tag_rules.min_severity (:2944), host_badges.scope (:3411), support_tickets.category/status (:3435-3437). Unconstrained: users.role (:292, values user/beta_tester/support/moderator/admin/super_admin plus the billing, security_analyst, content_manager and ops roles in STAFF_ROLES at lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:22), users.plan (:295), gifted_subscriptions.plan (:949), team_members.role (:898) and team_invites.role (:909), domains.status (:3178, whose 'verified' value is the gate that authorizes intrusive active probing, see lib/domains/scope.ts), scheduled_scans.frequency (:458), webhooks.type (:477), data_requests.status (:873), billing_history.status (:527), user_notifications.type (:1662), email_logs.status (:675), scan_history.source (:424) and .scan_type (:2076), users.auth_provider (:1878), .two_factor_method (:315), .subscription_status (:298) and .billing_interval (:2683). The concrete consequence is in lib/database/cleanup.ts:152-195: the per-plan scan retention runs four DELETEs whose WHERE clauses match the literals 'free' (or NULL), 'core_supporter', 'pro_supporter' and 'elite_supporter'. A users.plan value outside that set matches none of them, so those scans are retained forever with no error and no log line. lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:96 compounds it by casting an arbitrary column value straight to the enum type (`return effectivePlan as PlanType`) with no membership check, after which lib/billing/plan-limits.ts indexes PLAN_LIMIT_KEYS with it. Every current write path does validate (app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:1869-1880 for update_plan, :1652-1657 for gift_subscription, and the billing routes write literals or the output of getPlanFromProductId), so this is a latent constraint gap rather than a live bug: the paths that can introduce a bad value are the SQL repair scripts, scripts/restore-db.mjs, and hand-run SQL, all of which the self-hosting docs point operators at.
impact: The database does not enforce the value sets that authorization and money decisions are made from. A users.plan value outside the four known literals silently exempts that account's scan history from every retention rule in lib/database/cleanup.ts, so their data is kept forever with no error, and lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:96 hands the same unchecked string to the plan-limits resolver. A users.role value outside the known set fails closed for staff checks but is invisible in the admin panel, and a domains.status other than 'verified' or 'pending' is treated as unverified with no signal that the row is malformed. Every one of these is reachable through the documented self-hosted repair and restore scripts, which is precisely the situation a CHECK exists for.
recommendation: Add CHECK constraints for the five that carry real authorization or money semantics: users.role against the union of STAFF_ROLES plus user, beta_tester and super_admin; users.plan and gifted_subscriptions.plan against the four PlanId values in lib/billing/catalog.ts:12; team_members.role and team_invites.role against the team role set; domains.status against pending/verified/reverify_failed. Use the drop-and-recreate pattern already used for scan_tags_source_check at instrumentation.ts:2469-2475 so widening one later stays possible. Separately, make lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:96 validate membership before the cast and fall back to 'free' instead of casting blind, and make the cleanup retention in lib/database/cleanup.ts cover the else case rather than silently skipping it.

title: broadcast_recipients has no UNIQUE(message_id, user_id), so the mass-email send loop uses a read-then-insert guard that two concurrent sends both pass
description: broadcast_recipients (instrumentation.ts:1151-1162) has a surrogate `id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY` and two separate single-column indexes on message_id and user_id, and no uniqueness on the pair. The send handler and the resend handler each compensate in the application, with a comment that says so verbatim: "broadcast_recipients has no unique key, so this is an app-level guard rather than ON CONFLICT" (app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts:555-557 and the duplicated copy at :717-719). The guard is `SELECT 1 FROM broadcast_recipients WHERE message_id = $1 AND user_id = $2 AND status = 'sent' LIMIT 1` followed, if the select returned nothing, by sendEmail and then a plain INSERT (:559-573 and :721-735). Nothing serialises the two steps, and the same recipient is only marked after the SMTP round trip completes, so the window between the SELECT and the INSERT is the full duration of one email send. Two admins hitting send and resend for the same message, or one admin double-clicking, or the resend path racing a still-running first send, both pass the SELECT for the same recipient and both send.
impact: The whole verified user base can receive the same broadcast twice, from a feature whose stated design goal in that comment is that it must not. AUDIT-012#perf-07 already established that this loop iterates every verified user with no LIMIT and does one SELECT plus one INSERT plus one sequential SMTP call per recipient, so the race window per recipient is large and the number of recipients is unbounded. Duplicate mass email is the fastest way to get a sending domain reputation-flagged.
recommendation: Add `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_broadcast_recipients_message_user ON broadcast_recipients(message_id, user_id);` in instrumentation.ts and replace both read-then-insert blocks with an insert-first claim: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (message_id, user_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING id, send the email only when a row came back, then UPDATE the status. That also satisfies AUDIT-012#perf-15's item (8), which asked for a plain composite index on the same two columns for the read side, so one unique index covers both findings.

title: users.unsubscribe_token is the sole lookup key of a public unauthenticated endpoint and has neither an index nor a UNIQUE constraint
description: unsubscribe_token is added at instrumentation.ts:1248-1250 as `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS unsubscribe_token UUID DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()` with no NOT NULL, no UNIQUE, and no CREATE INDEX anywhere in the file (grep for the column name in instrumentation.ts returns only that one line). It is the only credential the unsubscribe flow has: app/api/v3/account/unsubscribe/route.ts:33 runs `SELECT id, email FROM users WHERE unsubscribe_token = $1` for the GET and :68 runs `SELECT id FROM users WHERE unsubscribe_token = $1` for the POST, both unauthenticated, and the token is embedded in every outbound notification email by lib/notifications/notifications.ts:98-105. Every other token column in the schema that identifies a row is declared UNIQUE (scan_history.share_token :425, team_invites.token :910, host_badges.badge_token :3362, staff_invites.token in lib/admin/staff-invites.ts:37) and most also carry an index. Collision is not realistic given the UUID default (the volatile default makes ADD COLUMN rewrite the table and evaluate gen_random_uuid per existing row, so every row gets a distinct value), but the database does not guarantee it and nothing prevents an out-of-band UPDATE or a restore from creating a duplicate, in which case `rows[0]` picks an arbitrary one of the two accounts and unsubscribes the wrong user.
impact: Both unsubscribe lookups sequentially scan the entire users table on every click of an unsubscribe link in any notification email, which is the one link in the product that must work reliably for CAN-SPAM and GDPR compliance. The uniqueness the code depends on to identify an account is a convention, not a constraint, on the one column the app trusts to authenticate an unauthenticated caller.
recommendation: In instrumentation.ts, next to the ALTER at :1248, add `UPDATE users SET unsubscribe_token = gen_random_uuid() WHERE unsubscribe_token IS NULL;` then `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_unsubscribe_token ON users(unsubscribe_token);`, following the same backfill-then-unique-index pattern already used for scan_history.public_id at :2609-2619. That fixes the sequential scan and the missing guarantee in one statement.

title: users.updated_at is exported as the account's last-modified timestamp in both GDPR data exports while roughly two dozen UPDATE paths never bump it
description: users.updated_at is `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW()` (instrumentation.ts:321) with no NOT NULL and no trigger; no table in the schema has an updated_at trigger, so the column is only correct where a hand-written `updated_at = NOW()` appears in the UPDATE. Eight sites do that (app/actions/stripe.ts:110, app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:1884, lib/billing/staff-plan.ts:94, :110, :149, instrumentation.ts:2725, and the two role-change paths). About two dozen do not, including every security-relevant one: `UPDATE users SET role = $1` (app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:652, :703, :718), `UPDATE users SET disabled_at = NOW()` and the re-enable (:898, :935), the entire 2FA lifecycle (app/api/v3/auth/2fa/setup/route.ts:69, :153, :187; 2fa/disable/route.ts:57; 2fa/email-setup/route.ts:55, :122; 2fa/backup-codes/route.ts:110; 2fa/verify/route.ts:180), OAuth link and unlink (app/api/v3/account/oauth/[provider]/route.ts:143, :150; account/discord/route.ts:240), the privacy toggles (account/privacy/route.ts:45, account/share-privacy/route.ts:59, account/posture-digest/route.ts:48) and every `UPDATE users SET stripe_customer_id` (app/actions/stripe.ts:130, :401, :614, :759). The column is nonetheless surfaced to users as fact: the admin export_data handler selects it at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:1275 and the self-service GDPR export selects it at app/api/v3/data-request/route.ts:129-131, in both cases as the account's last-updated timestamp.
impact: A user who exercises their right of access gets an updated_at that can be months stale, having missed their own 2FA enrolment, every role change, an account suspension and un-suspension, and every OAuth connection change. For an operator debugging "when did this account change", the column is misleading rather than merely absent, which is worse.
recommendation: Add one trigger function and attach it to the tables that expose updated_at, rather than auditing two dozen call sites: `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION set_updated_at() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN NEW.updated_at = NOW(); RETURN NEW; END $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;` then a `BEFORE UPDATE FOR EACH ROW` trigger on users, notification_preferences, discord_connections, github_connections, user_ai_configs, staff_activity and support_tickets. Add it to the boot block in instrumentation.ts guarded by CREATE OR REPLACE and DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS so it stays idempotent. While there, add NOT NULL to created_at and updated_at, which the newer tables already declare (compare :640 and :678 against :320).

title: users.email UNIQUE is case-sensitive, so the one-account-per-address invariant is a convention repeated across eight call sites rather than a database guarantee
description: `email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL` (instrumentation.ts:284) gives a case-sensitive unique index, so 'Alice@example.com' and 'alice@example.com' are two legal rows. Every read and write currently normalizes by hand: lib/database/db-utils.ts:40 (`[email.toLowerCase().trim()]`), lib/auth/auth.ts:287 for createUser, :355 and :387 for createOAuthUser, app/api/v3/auth/oauth/[provider]/callback/route.ts:155 before both the identity lookup and the collision check at :204, app/api/v3/admin/staff-invites/route.ts:61-63 before storing an invite email, and app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:129 for the per-email rate-limit key. That convention currently holds everywhere I checked, so this is a latent gap rather than a live bug, but it is enforced only by every author remembering it. app/api/v3/auth/staff-invite/[token]/route.ts:202 inserts `invite.email` straight into users with no normalization of its own; it is correct today only because the admin route lowercased the value before storing the invite. Two paths look up by raw email without a visible lowercase in the same file: app/api/v3/teams/members/route.ts:254 (`SELECT unsubscribe_token FROM users WHERE email = $1`) and app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts:543 (the broadcast segment filter `AND u.email = $1`).
impact: If any future write path forgets the lowercase, the resulting row is invisible to getUserByEmail, so that account can never sign in with a password and a second account can be created for the same human without tripping the UNIQUE constraint. The failure is silent at write time and only surfaces later as "I can't log in" plus two accounts for one address, which is expensive to untangle once billing and scan history exist under both.
recommendation: Replace the plain UNIQUE with a case-insensitive one in instrumentation.ts: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_email_lower ON users(lower(email));` (it also replaces the redundant idx_users_email from schema-05), keeping the existing constraint until the new index is verified. That makes the invariant a database guarantee, and it is also the index that would serve a lookup rewritten as `WHERE lower(email) = $1`.

title: Sixty-five suites index mockQuery.mock.calls positionally while the real 30-second module-level settings cache decides whether a settings query lands in that list, so running a single test with -t can fail a test that passes in a full run
description: lib/config/runtime-config.ts:64 caches the whole system_settings snapshot at module scope for TTL_MS = 30_000. Because vitest isolates per file but not per test, the first it() in a file that reaches a settings read issues a `SELECT key, value FROM system_settings` through the mocked pool and warms the snapshot; every later it() in the same file does not. Any test that then reads `mockQuery.mock.calls[0]` or `[1]` is reading a different call depending on which test ran first. Three suites document the hazard in their own comments and defend against it: tests/app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.test.ts:30-38 ("whichever test first reaches the Promise.all in the route would warm it and silently change how many pool.query calls, and in what order, every later test makes"), tests/lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.test.ts:33-36, and tests/app/api/v3/history/route.test.ts:17-28, which intercepts the settings SQL inside the mock instead. 36 files call invalidateSettingsCache(). Counted: 65 files mock @/lib/database/db, do not mock @/lib/config/runtime-config, never call invalidateSettingsCache, never intercept the system_settings query, and do index mock.calls positionally. vitest.config.ts declares no setupFiles, so every suite has to remember this by hand.
impact: Deterministic today only because vitest runs a file's tests in declaration order. The moment a developer narrows a run with `npx vitest run <file> -t "..."`, a different test warms the cache and the positional index points at the wrong query, producing a failure that does not reproduce in a full run. The same breaks if anyone enables sequence.shuffle or reorders tests during a refactor. The debugging cost is high because the failure looks like a real assertion failure about SQL.
recommendation: Add `setupFiles: ["tests/_setup.ts"]` to the test block in vitest.config.ts and have that file call `invalidateSettingsCache()` in a global beforeEach, so the snapshot is cold for every test in every suite. That removes the hazard for all 191 DB-mocking suites at once and lets the three hand-written guards be deleted.

title: validateApiKey compares the decrypted key with === and falls through to two unindexed full scans of api_keys on every failed lookup
description: Two issues in the same function. (1) After the O(1) locator lookup, the key itself is checked with a plain `if (decrypted === key)` at lib/api/api-keys.ts:350 and again at :374 -- a short-circuiting comparison on a secret, in a file that otherwise reaches for keyed HMAC and bcrypt. Everywhere else in the auth surface a secret compare uses timingSafeEqual: lib/auth/password-hash.ts:92,117, lib/auth/totp.ts:179, lib/auth/pending-2fa.ts:346, lib/auth/oauth-state.ts:137, lib/auth/ipv4-echo-token.ts:248, app/api/v3/auth/2fa/verify/route.ts:233, and the nonce check at app/api/v3/auth/oauth/[provider]/callback/route.ts:131. (2) When the locator query returns no match -- which is every request carrying a wrong or made-up key -- control falls through to the legacy backfill query at line 366 (`WHERE ak.key_locator IS NULL AND ak.key_encrypted IS NOT NULL`, decrypting each returned row) and then the bcrypt fallback at line 393 (`WHERE ak.key_hash IS NOT NULL AND ak.key_locator IS NULL AND ak.key_encrypted IS NULL`, running bcrypt.compare per row at cost 12). Neither predicate is indexable, so both are sequential scans of api_keys, and both run on every single unauthenticated bad-Bearer request against any of the ~15 Bearer routes.
impact: The timing side of this is largely academic (the locator already narrows the candidate set to one row and the key has 256 bits of entropy), but it is a gratuitous deviation from the rule the rest of this codebase follows. The scan side is concrete: an unauthenticated attacker sending garbage Bearer tokens forces two full table scans of api_keys per request at zero cost to themselves, and if any legacy bcrypt rows exist, one bcrypt-cost-12 verification per row per request -- roughly 250ms of CPU per legacy row, on a route with no rate limit in front of it.
recommendation: Replace both `decrypted === key` comparisons in lib/api/api-keys.ts (lines 350, 374) with a length-checked `timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(decrypted), Buffer.from(key))`. Guard the two legacy fallbacks so they only run when legacy rows can actually exist: cache a boolean from a one-time `SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM api_keys WHERE key_locator IS NULL)` at module scope (invalidated on the backfill UPDATE at line 378), and skip lines 366-410 entirely when it is false. Add a partial index `CREATE INDEX ON api_keys (id) WHERE key_locator IS NULL` in instrumentation.ts if the fallback must stay unconditional.

title: Three completion paths write rows one INSERT at a time where a single multi-row INSERT would do: crawl pages, AI verify verdicts, and boot-time migrations
description: (a) At the end of a crawl, `for (const pr of pageResults)` runs one `INSERT INTO scan_history (...) VALUES ($1...$12) RETURNING id` per page (lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:630-650) -- up to 250 sequential round trips on the Elite plan (lib/billing/crawl-page-limits.ts:23). (b) `lib/ai/verify-findings.ts:583-593` loops the verdict map and runs one `INSERT INTO scan_finding_feedback ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` per finding, routinely 50-300 sequential inserts. (c) Boot-time passes do the same: lib/billing/staff-plan.ts:265-268 (one query per staff row, driving SELECT at :254 unbounded), lib/auth/security-migration.ts:89-98 and :123-139 (one UPDATE per row), lib/uploads/avatar-migration.ts:120-151 and :194-214 (three queries per avatar). Note the correct pattern already exists in this codebase: `saveAutoTags` builds a single multi-row INSERT (lib/tags/auto-tags.ts:802-816).
impact: (a) adds 250 serialized round trips to the tail of a crawl the user is already waiting on. (b) adds one round trip per finding to the AI verify flow. (c) lengthens every process start, which matters because instrumentation.ts also runs the full schema DDL at boot.
recommendation: Replace each loop with one multi-row `INSERT ... VALUES (...),(...) RETURNING id` built the way lib/tags/auto-tags.ts:802-816 builds its parameter list, or with `UNNEST($1::type[], ...)` for the larger sets. For (c), a single `UPDATE ... FROM (VALUES ...)` replaces the per-row loops.

title: webhook_deliveries is written on every webhook event and never pruned, because lib/database/cleanup.ts has no retention rule for it
description: `lib/webhooks/delivery.ts:111` inserts a row into `webhook_deliveries` on every delivery attempt (and the module retries once on failure, so a failing webhook writes two rows per event). The table is created at instrumentation.ts:2328 with `idx_webhook_deliveries_webhook_id ON webhook_deliveries(webhook_id, attempted_at DESC)` (:2336). Grepping lib/database/cleanup.ts for `webhook_deliveries` returns nothing -- the retention pass that prunes sessions, rate_limits, tokens, scan_finding_feedback, user_notifications, github_review_usage, ai_conversations, email_logs, system_error_logs and admin_audit_log has no rule for it. AUDIT-011's drift-25 already noted this table has no reader; combined with no writer-side retention, it accumulates forever.
impact: A user with an active webhook on an hourly schedule writes ~24 rows a day per webhook, permanently. Nothing reads the table, so the growth is invisible until it shows up as disk usage and as backup/restore time on the self-hosted deployments this project targets.
recommendation: Either add a retention DELETE for `webhook_deliveries` to lib/database/cleanup.ts alongside the other log tables (with an admin-configurable retention setting matching the pattern used for email_logs), or, if AUDIT-011's drift-25 conclusion holds and the table genuinely has no consumer, stop writing it in lib/webhooks/delivery.ts:111 and drop it.

title: webhook_deliveries audit table is write-only -- nothing ever reads it
description: instrumentation.ts creates webhook_deliveries this session and lib/webhooks/delivery.ts writes to it correctly on every attempt, but no route or UI component ever selects from it. The partial index's shape (scoped to webhook_id, ordered by attempted_at DESC) strongly implies a delivery-history UI was intended but never built.
recommendation: Either add a GET delivery-history endpoint + UI, or note in code that this is intentionally admin/DB-only for now.

title: Downgrade plan leaves 4 performance indexes behind that the matching upgrade added
description: Live-verified: ran the real 3.0.0-to-2.0.0 downgrade against a migrated scratch DB. All 26 steps succeeded, restored the exact 34-table v2.0.0 set, no data loss. However idx_admin_audit_admin_created, idx_admin_audit_target_user, idx_api_usage_key_used, and idx_scan_history_user_scanned are absent from the downgrade's dropIndexes list and remain in place afterward. Cosmetic only, no data loss or functional break, but the downgraded schema isn't byte-for-byte identical to a true v2.0.0 install.
recommendation: Add the 4 missing index names to the downgrade export's dropIndexes list in 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs, matching how idx_scan_history_status_pending_running is already handled.

title: audit:v2-tables only validates the 15 legacy v1-to-v2 tables; a clean run proves nothing about tonight's v2.0.0-to-3.0.0 migration
description: Ran fresh: 0 issues, exactly as expected. But scripts/_lib/audit-v2-tables.mjs's hardcoded TABLES list only cross-checks instrumentation.ts against versions/_snippets.mjs (the 1.0.0-to-2.0.0 migration). It has zero awareness of 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs or any v3.0.0 table/column, so it cannot catch and does not catch the gap in migration-01.
recommendation: Extend audit-v2-tables.mjs (or add a sibling script) to also cross-check every v3.0.0-fingerprint table plus every CREATE TABLE/ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN in instrumentation.ts against 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs's addTables/addColumns, or clearly document that its 0-issues result only covers the frozen v1-to-v2 boundary.

title: Verified correct: no icon-only button without an accessible name, no onClick on a bare div, no positive tabIndex, every image has alt, and prefers-reduced-motion is honoured globally
description: Recorded so the next audit does not redo the work. (1) Icon-only buttons: a script walked every `
impact: None. Documented to narrow the search area for the next accessibility pass: the risk in this codebase is concentrated in the colour tokens (a11y-01 through a11y-03, a11y-05, a11y-10, a11y-18) and in the small set of hand-rolled components that bypass the shadcn/Radix primitives, not in the general component library.

title: Verified correct: all 71 pages have page-specific metadata, all 749 check descriptions are unique, the OG image is a correct 1200x630, and there is no indexable duplicate of a scan result
description: Recording what I verified as correct so the next audit does not re-derive it. (1) Metadata coverage is complete: I walked all 71 page.tsx files and resolved each to the nearest metadata source. Zero fall back to the root default. 45 use pageMetadata (indexable, canonical, OG, Twitter, googleBot directives), 25 use privatePageMetadata (noindex, nofollow, nocache), and the only inline case is app/page.tsx, which is a bare `redirect("/landing")` with no content of its own. (2) Hand-written copy is in range: across all 44 description strings and 61 title strings in app/**, zero titles exceed 60 characters with the " | VulnRadar" suffix, zero descriptions exceed 160 except one 163-character TechArticle description const at app/docs/api/playground/layout.tsx:11 (the meta description in the same file is 154), and no two pages share a description. (3) All 749 generated check descriptions are unique, and so are all 749 raw `description` fields in the checks-data JSON. (4) public/og-image.png is exactly 1200x630 at 107.6 KB, twitter.card is "summary_large_image" everywhere (lib/seo/metadata.ts:116), and metadataBase is set (app/layout.tsx:118) so relative image and canonical paths resolve absolute. (5) No indexable duplicate of a scan result exists: there is no /history/[id] page, and /shared/[token] and /host/[hostname] are both noindex, so the same report is never indexable at two URLs. (6) trailingSlash is not set in next.config.js, so Next 308-redirects /path/ to /path and there are no trailing-slash duplicates; the only query-parameter surface on an indexable page is /public-scans?page=N, which canonicalises to /public-scans. (7) The sitemap is 805 URLs (33 hand-listed, 18 categories, 5 alternatives, 749 checks), far under the 50,000-URL and 50 MB limits, so no sitemap index is needed yet. (8) /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt both exist as real routes (app/llms.txt/route.ts, app/llms-full.txt/route.ts) and are among the only 5 prerendered routes in the build. (9) Alt text is a non-issue for discoverability: there are 7 `` elements in all of app/ and components/, and the only one on an indexable page is inside a code sample in app/docs/sharing/page.tsx:386 which already carries an alt. (10) app/layout.tsx:177 renders SiteStructuredData without a nonce while every other JSON-LD call site passes one; this is cosmetic, since a `script type="application/ld+json"` is a data block that the HTML spec returns from before the CSP inline check, so it is not blocked.
impact: None. These are the checks a discoverability audit would otherwise repeat, and the SEO foundation here is genuinely above average for a project this size: a single pageMetadata helper, a routes.ts that derives the generated surfaces from the same loaders the pages use, real JSON-LD across six types, and llms.txt.
recommendation: No action. Use this as the baseline: the defects filed in seo-01 through seo-21 are the delta from an otherwise sound implementation, not a missing foundation.

title: Rollback coverage is complete at the version level but the 11 boot-only tables have no down step, so a downgrade leaves them behind as orphans
description: Answering the rollback question directly: every registered transition does have a down step. scripts/migrate/_registry.mjs:573 composes transitions pairwise across the three registry versions, findVersionFile (line 609) resolves 3.0.0 to 2.0.0 to 2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs (which exports `downgrade` at line 1169) and 2.0.0 to 1.0.0 to 2.0.0-to-1.0.0.mjs, so there is no missing rollback path. The gap is the same one as migrate-01 seen from the other direction: because the 11 boot-only tables are created by no upgrade step, the downgrade's dropTables list (line 1204-1230) does not include them either, so a 3.0.0 to 2.0.0 downgrade leaves browserbase_credit_purchases, browserbase_usage, domains, email_logs, github_credit_purchases, scan_screenshots, support_tickets, support_ticket_messages, support_ticket_shares, user_avatars and worker_failure_state in place. All 11 have FKs to users or scan_history with ON DELETE CASCADE or SET NULL, so the downgrade's `DELETE FROM users WHERE password_hash IS NULL` (line 1293) does not error on them, and a subsequent 2.0.0 to 1.0.0 downgrade does not error either.
impact: No failure and no data loss, but a downgraded database ends up as a mixture: it fingerprints as 2.0.0 (fingerprintDetect only requires the fingerprint's tables to be present, scripts/migrate/_detect.mjs:33) while carrying 11 v3.7-era tables full of live data that the v2 app cannot read and that nothing will clean up. Also worth recording that the destructive-step counter shown before an upgrade (migrate.mjs:479) is driven only by dropTable and dropColumn kinds, so on the 2.0.0 to 3.0.0 upgrade it reports exactly one destructive step (the year_month DROP COLUMN at line 1134) and the upgrade path therefore never prompts for anything meaningful.
recommendation: Fold into migrate-01's fix: when the 11 tables are added to addTables, add the same names to dropTables in the downgrade, ordered so children (support_ticket_messages, support_ticket_shares) precede parents (support_tickets). The DROP TABLE ... CASCADE that _planner.mjs:92 already emits handles the rest.

title: Column types are inconsistent for the same kind of value across tables: IP addresses in three different types, and two JSON payloads stored as TEXT
description: The schema stores an IP address three different ways: `INET` in security_alerts.ip_address (instrumentation.ts:1100), `VARCHAR(45)` in sessions (:336), sessions.ipv4_address (:352), api_keys.bound_ip (:382), admin_audit_log (:574), device_trust (:856) and access_rules (implicitly, in the TEXT `value` column at :1009), and plain `TEXT` in staff_activity.ip_address (:736). Only the INET column can be compared with a subnet operator or validated by the database; the VARCHAR ones silently accept anything up to 45 characters, which matters for api_keys.bound_ip because lib/api/api-keys.ts's passesApiKeyIpBinding compares it as a string. Two JSON payloads are stored as TEXT while everything else in the schema uses JSONB: `users.backup_codes TEXT` (:316), which is written with JSON.stringify (app/api/v3/auth/2fa/backup-codes/route.ts:110) and read with JSON.parse (:49), and which app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:156 probes with the string comparison `u.backup_codes IS NOT NULL AND u.backup_codes != '[]'` to compute has_backup_codes, so any serialization that emits `[ ]` or `null` instead of exactly `[]` flips that flag; and `data_requests.data TEXT` (:874), which holds the whole GDPR export document. Positives worth recording, since they are the things that usually go wrong: money is integer cents everywhere (billing_history.amount_cents INTEGER at :525, all three credit ledgers use BIGINT token counts), there is no float anywhere in the schema, and every timestamp is TIMESTAMPTZ or TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE with no naked `timestamp` column, so there is no time-zone ambiguity to fix.
impact: No current failure. The cost is that a query cannot mix these columns (you cannot join or compare security_alerts.ip_address against sessions.ip_address without a cast), no CIDR or subnet analysis is possible over the VARCHAR ones, and the has_backup_codes flag in the admin user detail view depends on exact string equality with '[]' rather than on a structural check the database could do.
recommendation: Low priority, but when any of these tables is next touched: migrate staff_activity.ip_address to VARCHAR(45) to match its six siblings (or migrate all seven to INET, which is the better target and lets the admin panel do subnet queries), and convert users.backup_codes and data_requests.data to JSONB so app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:156 can use `jsonb_array_length(backup_codes) > 0` instead of comparing text to '[]'. Both conversions are `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE jsonb USING col::jsonb`, safe on existing rows since both already contain valid JSON.
